metadata.title: Platonic geodesic trees in the $K-$Space
metadata.abstract: In this paper, We prove that: (A) If $m\ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges (geodesic segments), which form $m$ platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ and $(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}-m)$ platonic angles with measure $90^{o}.$ (Existence of a Fermat Coordinate system) (B) If $m=2,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree with three vertices and 2 edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ or $150^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$ (Minimal spanning geodesic tree). (C) If $m=3,$ there exists a Platonic tree and the Steiner point is identical with the Fermat point, having three edges, which meet at $120^{\circ}$ (Hexagonal coordinate system). (D) If $m$ is even and $m \ge 4,$ there exists a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form platonic angles with only two distinct measures $90^{o}$ and $180^{\circ}.$ (Existence of a Cartesian coordinate system). (E) If $m\ge 4$, there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges , which form only platonic angles with measure $120^{o}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system). (F) If $m\ge 3,$ there does not exist a Platonic geodesic tree having $m$ edges, which form platonic angles with only one measure $150^{o},$ or two distinct measures $120^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ or two distinct measures $90^{\circ}$ and $150^{\circ}$ (Non existence of a Fermat coordinate system). A classification of platonic geodesic trees with boundary vertex set $V$ and added vertex set $Q$ in the $K-$Space is given by conditions (A), (B), (C), (D), (E), (F), which characterize each vertex in $V\cup Q.$

metadata.title: Breaking the Fourth Wall: The Planar Centroid Banach--Mazur Diameter Is Strictly Less than $4$
metadata.abstract: We prove that the centroid Banach--Mazur diameter of planar convex bodies is strictly less than $4$, (slightly) improving the prior upper bound $69/17\approx 4.05882$ due to Lassak. The proof combines a sharp covariance-ellipse sandwich, whose equality cases in any single direction occur only for triangles, with a compactness argument: an extremal pair at distance $4$ would consist of two triangles, which are linearly equivalent and hence must in fact be at distance $1$. The resulting gap below $4$ is uniform but nonquantitative.

metadata.title: On the Reverse Projection Inequality
metadata.abstract: In \cite {ChenFengLiXiXu2026}, a reverse projection inequality for general convex bodies was established in three dimensions. In this paper, we completely characterize the equality cases of this inequality. We further show that the reverse projection inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq9$. The counterexamples are constructed as full-dimensional polytopes with at most $n+2$ facets.

metadata.title: Certified Geometry and Admissible Motion of Gerver's Sofa
metadata.abstract: The moving sofa problem asks for the largest planar set that can pass through a unit-width right-angled hallway. Gerver's 1992 construction remains the largest explicit example, but its defining switching parameters, continuum of supporting hallways, and contact topology involve transcendental equations and global inequalities. We give a reproducible exact-rational certification of the construction. A strict four-dimensional Krawczyk inclusion encloses the reduced switching system, while an independent twenty-two-dimensional Krawczyk calculation verifies Romik's full matching and contact equations in an explicit rational box. Exact interval propagation through the five analytic phases proves the support identities, global half-plane constraints, inner-wall separation, niche topology, oriented contacts, injectivity, and area bounds. From the certified support functions we identify every supporting hallway as L_t=x(t)+R_tL. For G=K_0\setminus\mathcal N(K_0) we prove directly that G is nonempty, closed, and connected and that \Phi_t(q)=R_{-t}(q-x(t)) is a continuous path in SE(2) carrying G through the hallway, with the correct initial and final arms. We further identify G with Romik's reconstruction of Gerver's classical eighteen-piece sofa. The deterministic companion verifier uses only Python's standard library and exact rational arithmetic. As a consequence, the Gerver-specific geometric hypotheses in Baek's recent variational framework are rigorously certified; we also clarify the one-sided tangent-speed convention at two contact-curve junctions.
metadata.comment: 22 pages. Includes a deterministic exact-rational companion verifier and independent 4-dimensional and 22-dimensional Krawczyk certificates

metadata.title: $L_p$-Integral Affine Surface Area-Variational Capacity Inequalities
metadata.abstract: For $n\geq 2$ and $1<p<n$, Ludwig-Xiao-Zhang \cite{LXYZ} asked whether the $L_p$-integral affine surface area of every convex body containing the origin in its interior is bounded above by the ball-normalized multiple of \(L_p\)-variational capacity, and whether the analogous analytic inequality holds for $L_p$-convexified level sets. We answer both questions negatively.

metadata.title: Thirteen Results in Magnitude Theory
metadata.abstract: We prove thirteen results concerning three aspects of magnitude theory. The first four concern small-scale magnitude and microscopic weightings. We identify the derivative of the magnitude function at the origin with maximal energy, allowing the value $+\infty$, and construct finite spaces for which small-scale magnitude diverges or for which the one-point property and finite concentration do not produce a microscopic weighting. A fifth result disproves the conjectured monotonicity of magnitude by giving a fourteen-point metric space of strict negative type whose magnitude function decreases. The remaining eight results concern continuity and dimension. Magnitude is Hausdorff-continuous at finite subsets of finite-dimensional positive definite normed spaces, but need not be continuous on compact subsets, even under convexity, geodesicity, bounded tractability, or simultaneous Hausdorff and Lipschitz convergence. The same constructions disprove an $\ell_1$-intrinsic-volume formula and two tractability conjectures. Finally, we construct a countable compact space of negative type whose Minkowski dimension is zero and whose lower and upper magnitude dimensions are both infinite.

metadata.title: Necessary and Sufficient Criteria for the Realizability of Kaleidocycles Composed of Six Congruent Isosceles Tetrahedra
metadata.abstract: A classical kaleidocycle is a closed cyclic chain of congruent, edge-hinged tetrahedra with successive hinge axes at right angles, capable of continuous inside-out motion. Kaleidocycles composed of six isosceles tetrahedra (disphenoids) form a natural generalization in which consecutive hinge axes need not be perpendicular. Their kinematics are governed by the closure equation for threefold-symmetric Bricard 6R linkages. We derive a new compact closure equation directly from threefold symmetry using the composition of rotations, and show its equivalence to the classical formulation. Furthermore, we establish two equivalent necessary and sufficient criteria for a kaleidocycle to admit continuous, unblocked motion in terms of the geometric parameters of the constituent disphenoid. These criteria yield sharp bounds on the admissible geometric parameters of realizable kaleidocycles. Finally, we study assemblies of eight such kaleidocycles joined face-to-face. We identify a configuration exhibiting full octahedral symmetry, which forms a polyhedral structure closely related to the disdyakis dodecahedron.

metadata.title: A Power-Diagram Upper Bound for Twenty-Six Variable-Radius Disks in a Square
metadata.abstract: Let $S_{26}$ denote the supremum of the sum of the radii of 26 pairwise interior-disjoint closed disks of positive radius contained in the unit square. We prove $2.635983084917607783\ldots \le S_{26}\le \sqrt{\frac{2577}{2500}+\frac{11}{\sqrt3}}=2.716919756099889566\ldots$. The lower bound is accompanied by an exact rational feasibility certificate. For the upper bound, we assign the disks their clipped power cells, convert cell area into a reciprocal exterior-angle cost, and combine this local inequality with Euler side counts. The extremal case for the resulting relaxation has four boundary transitions and a four-cell boundary cycle; its continuous angle allocation is reduced to a concave one-variable problem. All finite numerical inequalities are rigorously enclosed by a reproducible certificate. metadata.title: A 0.41275 lower bound for the three-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem
metadata.abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ of constant width $w>0$ satisfies \[ \operatorname{Vol}(K)\ge \frac{1651}{4000}w^3=0.41275\,w^3. \] This improves the certified lower bound $0.411040473721188\ldots\,w^3$ announced by Hyra and the earlier spectral bound $4\pi w^3/33$ of Nishioka. The main new ingredient is a contact-tetrahedron estimate near equality in Jung's circumradius inequality. Four balanced contacts of a minimum circumscribed ball form a near-regular tetrahedron; constant width then forces, beyond the tetrahedron itself, spherical regions over its faces, spindle sectors along its edges, and additional face-edge sectors. These regions can be selected with pairwise disjoint interiors and quantified by the total squared-edge deficit. A sharp convexity argument relates that deficit to the circumradius, and a symmetrization argument controls the four face contributions with only quadratic loss. This gives the analytic bound $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41275318$ near the Jung endpoint. For the complementary circumradius range we use Hyra's radial transport/tangent-majorant mechanism together with closed-form contact and antipodal profiles. The antipodal contribution has an elementary primitive. For the contact contribution, a second-order concavity estimate converts the angular Jacobian into an explicit rational lower density; that density is monotone in the circumradius. The whole intermediate range therefore reduces to a single endpoint calculation, giving $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41275168$. For smaller circumradius the tangent-majorant inequality with its nonnegative gap discarded already gives $\operatorname{Vol}(K)>0.41308109$. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted certificate.

metadata.title: Jensen's inequality on parity classes of jump M-convex functions
metadata.abstract: We prove Jensen's inequality on each coordinatewise parity class of a jump $M$-convex function on $\mathbb{Z}^n$, without assuming strong base orderability or a finite effective domain. If a finite convex combination of domain points has its barycenter in the same parity class, then the barycenter belongs to the domain and satisfies Jensen's inequality. We also prove that every domain point admits an affine support on its entire parity class. The set of support vectors is characterized by at most $3^n-1$ local inequalities, which yield optimality certificates, attained duality, and an exact formula for linear growth and stability under linear perturbations. The same conclusions hold for distributions with finite first moment supported on domain points of a single parity class, provided their mean lies in that class. We characterize equality by contact sets and give a quantitative bound on the Jensen gap. The proof combines induction on dimension with the known closure under infimal convolution: convolution with an even-box indicator gives finite-domain supports, a quadratic kernel proves barycenter feasibility, and a fixed local kernel yields global supports. A two-dimensional example shows that total parity alone does not suffice.

metadata.title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
metadata.abstract: Surround a unit ball with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders, each touching the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more such cylinder be added, for a total of $n+1$, if we are allowed to rearrange the configuration? We prove that the answer is ``no'' for $3\le n\le 7$, and ``yes'' if $n\geq 9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$, where the cylinders are the same size as the ball, is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, resolved recently. We also make progress on a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman, confirming the first decimal digit of their predicted value for the largest radius of four non-overlapping cylinders that touch a ball.

metadata.title: An Improved Lower Bound for Packing 203 Equal Spheres in a Unit Cube
metadata.abstract: This paper reports an improved numerical lower bound for packing 203 equal spheres in a unit cube. Let r denote the maximum common radius of equal non-overlapping spheres that can be packed in a unit cube. For N = 203, the configuration currently listed in Packomania has a feasible radius of approximately r = 0.088145402159. Starting from this public configuration, we perform further numerical optimization and obtain a new feasible configuration with r > 0.088145634693. The final configuration is checked by an independent verification program using 100-digit arithmetic. All 20503 sphere-pair constrains and all 1218 sphere-wall constraints are satisfied. The coordinates of the new configuration and the related programs are provided as supplementary material.

metadata.title: A Counterexample to Three Conjectures of Luo
metadata.abstract: We give a single counterexample to Conjectures 1--3 as stated in Luo's paper: a minimal two-tetrahedron triangulation of the lens space L(3,1) with a null-homotopic loop edge. metadata.title: Equilateral sets in $\ell_p^n$ beyond $n+1$: Linear excess and dimension cost
metadata.abstract: How many equilateral points can $\ell_p^n$ contain beyond $n+1$? For every fixed real $p>4$, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond $n+1$ grows at least linearly with $n$. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is $n+1$ at all sufficiently large finite $p$, with an explicit threshold. The least dimension admitting any fixed number of extra points is $p^{1+o(1)}$ as $p\to\infty$. The constructions and finite bounds are formalised in Lean. Thus $p=4$ marks the boundary: $n+1$ is exact in every dimension for $2\leq p\leq4$, while at every fixed finite $p>4$ the excess grows at least linearly with dimension.

metadata.title: Triangles and quadrilaterals suffice
metadata.abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Robert J. Lang over 20 years ago, stating that in a circle-packed origami design, any axial polygon with 5 or more sides can be reduced by properly adding a new circle. The proof is based on the structure of the medial axis of the region enclosed by the circles, and yields a concrete algorithm for finding the added circle. The result extends to configurations involving rivers.

analysisBasis.abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Robert J. Lang over 20 years ago, stating that in a circle-packed origami design, any axial polygon with 5 or more sides can be reduced by properly adding a new circle. The proof is based on the structure of the medial axis of the region enclosed by the circles, and yields a concrete algorithm for finding the added circle. The result extends to configurations involving rivers.

metadata.title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
metadata.abstract: Problem 73 on Green's list of open problems asks whether a smooth submanifold of codimension two in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must meet some affine two-plane in five points when $n$ is large. In this paper, we answer this question for every $n \geq 6$. Every nonempty relatively open subset of such a submanifold contains the vertices of an affinely regular pentagon, and the bound $n \geq 6$ is sharp for affinely regular pentagons. More generally, for every prime $p \geq 5$, the graph of a continuous map from a ball in $\mathbb{R}^{p-1}$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an affinely regular $p$-gon. A second argument gives six coplanar points when $n \geq 7$. Both proofs find the points by making the low Fourier modes of the graph map vanish along a circle.

metadata.title: Sharp Antipode-Neighbor Bounds in Every Dimension
metadata.abstract: Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ be finite with $\operatorname{diam}(P)\le1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, let $\mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at most $\varepsilon$, including the diagonal, and let $\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P)$ denote the number of ordered pairs at distance at least $1-\varepsilon$. We prove the sharp bound \[ \mathcal N_\varepsilon(P)\gtrsim_d \varepsilon^{(d-1)/2}\mathcal A_\varepsilon(P) \] conjectured by Steinerberger (2025). More generally, the same inequality holds for finite positive Borel measures. The main input is a uniform $L^2$ estimate, at cap thickness comparable to lattice spacing, for a supporting-direction incidence operator. In gnomonic coordinates, this operator is controlled by an incidence estimate for small Fenchel--Young gaps.

metadata.title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
metadata.abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.

metadata.title: Maximal volumes of pyramids in the unit cube
metadata.abstract: Let $Q_n=[0,1]^n$, $n\ge2$. Denote by $M_n$ be the maximal volume of a pyramid in $Q_n$ whose base is a hyperplane section of $Q_n$, and by $M_n^0$ the corresponding maximum when the section contains the center of $Q_n$. We prove that $nM_n<(n+1)M_{n+1}^0$.

metadata.title: An upper bound for the three-dimensional moving sofa problem in a snaky corridor
metadata.abstract: Let $K_M \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the "snaky" corridor with unit-square cross-section: an infinite entry arm parallel to the $x$-axis, a middle arm parallel to the $y$-axis whose clear straight section has length $M$, and an infinite exit arm parallel to the $z$-axis, with the two turns lying in the $x$-$y$ and $y$-$z$ planes. Let $V^*(K_M)$ be the supremum of the volumes of connected bodies that can be moved continuously (by rigid motions) from the entry arm to the exit arm while remaining inside $K_M$. We prove $V^*(K_M) \le 7.8691$ for every $M \ge 3.53$ (Theorem A); by a sharper analysis of the same mechanism, $V^*(K_M) \le 4.2862$ for every $M \ge 2.61$ (Theorem B); and, by replacing the final analytic caps with a certified branch-and-bound computation over the compact family of entry tubes compatible with the forced events, $V^*(K_M) \le 3.4083$ for every $M > 2.2$ (Theorem C; computer-assisted, in double precision with conservative slack). In particular all three bounds apply to the corridor with $M = 4$ used in Problem 6.64 of Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner ( arXiv:2511.02864 ), and uniformly to every "turns far apart" reading of that problem. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first upper bound for the snaky-corridor 3D moving sofa problem; previously not even finiteness of $V^*$ had been recorded. This note proves upper bounds only; combined with the certified lower bound 1.8558404 from the author's separate certification work via the problem's own evaluation pipeline, the state of the problem becomes $1.8558404 \le V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$. Theorems A and B are elementary and self-contained: a first-crossing (elbow) event forces a definite tilt of the body's own entry tube, and Fubini-type chord estimates for tilted tubes cap the volume. Theorem C certifies, by the same forced-event skeleton, the largest corridor volume that any admissible entry tube can carry.

metadata.title: New certified lower bounds for the moving sofa problem in a three-dimensional snaky corridor
metadata.abstract: Consider the "snaky" corridor $K_4 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ from Problem 6.64 of arXiv:2511.02864 : a tube of unit-square cross-section whose two right-angle turns lie in perpendicular planes, with a straight middle section of clear length $4$. We exhibit explicit rigid motions of connected bodies through $K_4$ and certify their volumes with the problem's own evaluation pipeline, unmodified, at the tight motion tolerances of its final scoring stage (translation $0.005$, rotation $0.05$ degrees). The certificates give $V^*(K_4) \ge 1.8355162$ at grid fineness $0.002$ and $V^*(K_4) \ge 1.8558404$ at grid fineness $0.001$, against the previously reported $1.81$; rerunning the pipeline's published best path under the identical configuration yields $1.8179428$, so every comparison is path against path under one fixed certifier. Three stages produce the record motion: a simple "staggered twist" backbone in which the whole 90-degree twist about the tube axis happens inside the second turn; evolutionary (CMA-ES) refinement, including a mixed-fidelity scheme that re-scores each generation's leading candidates on a grid twice as fine and lets those ranks steer recombination; and a gradient polish carried out directly at the finer carve resolution, guarded by periodic rebuilding of the frozen interpolation structure and by a penalty on control-pose spacing. These guards close three documented failure modes in which an optimizer inflates its own objective: frozen-structure inflation, spacing stretch, and exploitation of a coarse grid by optimizing and selecting on it. A staircase-based predictor with two grid bases, anchored by matching grid sensitivity, forecast the certificates to about $0.001$ before the runs. With the companion note's upper bound $V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$, the problem now sits in the bracket $1.8558404 \le V^*(K_4) \le 3.4083$. All paths, notebooks and certified results are public.

metadata.title: Upper bounds for Jung constants of $\ell_1^d$
metadata.abstract: For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that each nonempty bounded set in real $\ell_1^{4k+1}$ has an ambient enclosing ball of radius at most $(4k-1)/(4k)$ times its diameter. The bound is sharp in dimension five: $J(\ell_1^5)=3/4$. If a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$ exists, then $J(\ell_1^{4k-1})=J(\ell_1^{4k})=J(\ell_1^{4k+1})=(4k-1)/(4k)$. The upper bound for every $k\ge1$ has been formalized in Lean.

analysisBasis.abstract: For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that each nonempty bounded set in real $\ell_1^{4k+1}$ has an ambient enclosing ball of radius at most $(4k-1)/(4k)$ times its diameter. The bound is sharp in dimension five: $J(\ell_1^5)=3/4$. If a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$ exists, then $J(\ell_1^{4k-1})=J(\ell_1^{4k})=J(\ell_1^{4k+1})=(4k-1)/(4k)$. The upper bound for every $k\ge1$ has been formalized in Lean.

metadata.title: A Proof of the Analytic Entropy Conjecture
metadata.abstract: We prove that the geodesic flow of a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy if it admits globally defined, real-analytic Liouville integrals. This proves a longstanding conjecture proposed by Bolsinov and Taimanov.

metadata.title: An Explicit Bound for the First Dirichlet Eigenvalue via Two Moments
metadata.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\ge2$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth nonempty boundary, $\operatorname{Ric}_M\ge(n-1)Kg$ for $K>0$, and nonnegative outward boundary mean curvature. We derive an explicit algebraic lower bound $B_\eta$ for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue from Kasue's mixed inradius model. With $R$ the inradius and $s=4KR^2/\pi^2$, the bound involves one square root and approximates the model eigenvalue with relative error $O_n(s^4)$ as $s\downarrow0$ for fixed $n$. The construction uses the first two moments of a positive representation of the averaged model potential and a sharp pointwise corrector estimate. For the chosen spectral transfer, the first two moments determine an optimal bound. We also show that the model eigenvalue is the geometric infimum at fixed $(n,K,R)$. For $0<s<1$, it is approached by smooth collapsing balls with sectional curvature at least $K$ and totally geodesic boundary. At the maximal inradius, the model value is attained by the round hemisphere. The bound strictly improves the variance refinement throughout $0<s\le1$. We also give a direct algebraic comparison with an optimized power-test benchmark.

metadata.title: Distinguished bases and the braid group action for solutions of the tt*-Toda equations
metadata.abstract: We implement (in a concrete example) a procedure of Dubrovin which gives a braid group action on spaces of solutions of ordinary differential equations such as the quantum differential equation of complex projective space. Such actions originated in physics for the tt* (topological-antitopological fusion) equations. We make the procedure systematic by utilizing an algebraic description of braid group actions on distinguished bases. We also generalize to the case of (arbitrary) solutions of the tt*-Toda equations, one of which corresponds to the quantum cohomology of complex projective space.

metadata.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
metadata.abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.

metadata.title: Tight surgeries on torus knots
metadata.abstract: We give a complete classification of tight contact structures on manifolds obtained from any surgery along any torus knot, which provides the first such classification on an infinite family of knots. The main tools are the classification of non-loose torus knots, bordered contact invariants via their immersed curve interpretations, and non-thickenable tori in knot complements. As a byproduct of this classification, we also give the first classification of contact structures on some surface bundles over the circle with fibers of genus larger than $1$. The symplectic fillability of these contact structures is also studied and leads to, among other things, the disproof of a conjecture of Ghiggini and Van Horn-Morris on Stein fillability of some contact structures on a Brieskorn sphere.

metadata.title: An Abresch-Rosenberg type tensor and a gap theorem for CMC hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$
metadata.abstract: We construct a symmetric trace-free tensor for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ that extends the Abresch-Rosenberg tensor. Within its natural class, it is characterized by the linearity of its Codazzi defect, and its complete connected zero set consists exactly of the rotational CMC spheres. An exact integrated Simons identity yields explicit gap theorems, valid for every $h>1$ in $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and every $h>(n\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^{n-1}r\,dr)^{-1}$ in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$. We compare the pinching thresholds with the pointwise algebraic level that implies convexity. In $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the explicit pinching conditions imply strict convexity, so there the method gives an independent proof with explicit constants. In $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the pinching region exceeds the convexity level for $n\in\{3,4\}$ and every admissible $h$, and for $n\geq5$ whenever $h^2\geq n/(6(n+2))$; there the gap theorem does not require convexity to be known in advance. We also determine second-order large-$h$ asymptotics of the thresholds.

metadata.title: Asymptotically conical shrinking ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow: rotational construction and uniqueness
metadata.abstract: For $1\leq r\leq n-1$ we study shrinking self-similar ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow, $S_r=c\langle X,N\rangle$ with $c<0$, that are asymptotic to a cone. For every rotational cone of positive slope we construct a smooth embedded rotational end and prove that its profile is the only positive solution of the profile equation with the prescribed slope at infinity. Its angular defect $xu'-u$ is strictly negative, which yields $r$-admissibility, and the profile has a complete asymptotic expansion for $u(x)/x$ in powers of $x^{-(r+1)}$, valid after arbitrary differentiation. The profiles depend real analytically on the slope and, on sufficiently distant exterior regions, foliate the image of the corresponding family. Our main result removes the symmetry assumption: two ends that converge smoothly, with multiplicity one, to the same circular cone coincide outside a compact set. The proof transforms the equation for their difference into an almost-eigenfunction inequality for a drift Laplacian on an auxiliary conical metric and applies Bernstein's asymptotic analysis on weakly conical ends. The argument extends to strictly $r$-admissible cones whose links have constant principal curvatures.

metadata.title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
metadata.abstract: A classical uniformization theorem of Ahlfors from 1963 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipscitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a large class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipscitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a large class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

metadata.title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
metadata.abstract: Let $\Phi$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $\mu\leq\lambda$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(\Phi,\mu,\lambda)$ the convex polytope $$P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda} = (\mu+C)\cap(\lambda-C)\cap(\overline{D}-\rho),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\Phi^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^{\Phi}_{\mu,\lambda}$ and $P^{\Phi'}_{\mu',\lambda'}$ are isometric, then $$K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)=K^{\Phi'}_{\lambda'\mu'}(q),$$ where $K^{\Phi}_{\lambda\mu}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $\mu$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(\lambda)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

metadata.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
metadata.abstract: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. metadata.title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
metadata.abstract: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $°p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=\alpha\,q(\beta z+h)+k$ or $p(z)=\alpha\,\bar q(\beta z+h)+k$ for some $\alpha,\beta,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.

metadata.title: The Height of Choe's Higher-Dimensional Enneper Surface
metadata.abstract: We prove that Choe's higher-dimensional Enneper hypersurfaces in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $3\le n\le6$, cannot be confined between two parallel hyperplanes, disproving his slab confinement conjecture. We further strengthen this conclusion by determining their precise height growth exponent. If $H(R)$ denotes the maximal absolute height above the asymptotic hyperplane within the horizontal ball of radius $R$, then $H(R)=R^{\alpha_1+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$, where $\alpha_1=\frac{\sqrt{(n-2)^2+4\lambda_1(\Omega)}-(n-2)}{2}$, $\Omega=S^{n-1}\setminus[0,\infty)^n$, and $\lambda_1(\Omega)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the spherical Laplacian. In particular, $0<\alpha_1<1$, so the height is unbounded but grows sublinearly. The proof combines the blow-down behavior of a fundamental piece of Choe's hypersurface with the rigidity of positive harmonic functions on cones. In dimension two, the formula gives $2/3$, recovering the classical Enneper height-growth exponent.

metadata.title: Volume growth and parabolicity for non-symmetric operators
metadata.abstract: The interplay between a weighted volume measure and its naturally associated weighted Laplace operator is fundamental to the geometric analysis of weighted structures governed by gradient vector fields. Beyond the gradient setting, however, the theory has remained considerably less developed, largely because this natural correspondence is lost. In this paper, we identify invariant measures as the appropriate framework for extending the theory to general drifted Laplace operators. This approach yields a systematic treatment of parabolicity in the non-gradient setting, reveals its connection with volume growth, and leads to new volume finiteness results for non-gradient geometric structures.

metadata.title: Lattices with Large Kissing Number from Local Density
metadata.abstract: Let $\kappa_p(n)$ denote the maximum kissing number of a lattice $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that $\kappa_p(n) \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$ for all $p\ge 1$ and that $\kappa_p(n) \geq \Omega(\alpha_p^n)$ for all $p > 2$, where $\alpha_p > 1$ is a constant depending only on $p$. In particular, our former result improves on the previously best known lower bound of $\kappa_2(n) \geq 2^{\Theta(\log^2 n)}$ for the $\ell_2$ kissing number, which has stood for over $60$ years. (In concurrent and independent work, Laarhoven and Kominers [arXiv, 2026] showed a similar lower bound on $\kappa_2(n)$ using similar techniques.) In fact, our lower bounds follow from efficient (randomized) constructions of lattices with large kissing number. Our results use a general construction of lattices with large kissing number. Specifically, we show a simple equivalence between such lattices and a new object that we call an exact locally dense lattice. Closely related objects appear throughout the literature on computational lattice problems. Our constructions of lattices with large kissing number then follow as corollaries by showing that constructions due to Bennett and Peikert [RANDOM, 2023] (using Craig lattices) and Aggarwal and Stephens-Davidowitz [STOC, 2018] (using sparsification of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) in fact give exact locally dense lattices, as well as a new construction of exact locally dense lattices built from rotations of the $m$-dimensional checkerboard lattice $D_m$.

metadata.title: Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework
metadata.abstract: This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincaré-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.

metadata.title: Localization of Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
metadata.abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.

metadata.title: Rigidity of Immersed Gauss Curvature Shrinkers in Euclidean Space
metadata.abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that any connected closed oriented smooth immersion $X:M^m\to\mathbb{R}^{m+1}$ satisfying \[ K=\left\langle X,\nu\right\rangle \] is an embedding onto the unit sphere. No convexity is assumed. At a point maximizing $|X|$, we find a strictly convex component of $\{K>0\}$. If this component does not coincide with $M$, its polar immersion bounds an unbounded convex set. A finite area lemma then extends the local surface area formula for the polar body to a global measure identity. Using the vanishing first moment of surface area measure, we show that the origin lies in the interior of the polar body, contradicting the existence of recession directions. Thus the hypersurface is strictly convex, and the classification of strictly convex shrinkers completes the proof.

analysisBasis.abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that any connected closed oriented smooth immersion $X:M^m\to\mathbb{R}^{m+1}$ satisfying \[ K=\left\langle X,\nu\right\rangle \] is an embedding onto the unit sphere. No convexity is assumed. At a point maximizing $|X|$, we find a strictly convex component of $\{K>0\}$. If this component does not coincide with $M$, its polar immersion bounds an unbounded convex set. A finite area lemma then extends the local surface area formula for the polar body to a global measure identity. Using the vanishing first moment of surface area measure, we show that the origin lies in the interior of the polar body, contradicting the existence of recession directions. Thus the hypersurface is strictly convex, and the classification of strictly convex shrinkers completes the proof.

metadata.title: Shake concordance in the topological concordance class of the Hopf link

metadata.title: Orbit stratifications and smooth topology of positively curved six-manifolds with rank-one nonabelian symmetry
metadata.abstract: We study closed simply connected six-manifolds with positive sectional curvature and an effective isometric action of $SO(3)$ or $SU(2)$. Starting from Liu's corrected orbit-space analysis, we refine the stratification and recover smooth topology in several previously unresolved cases. For a boundaryless $SO(3)$ quotient, singular isotropy is connected, the weighted nonprincipal graph belongs to nine necessary families, and every action with only cyclic exceptional isotropy is classified equivariantly. The remaining branching families admit explicit rational intersection and Pontryagin formulas. For a three-ball $SO(3)$ quotient, the uniform-boundary configurations give sphere bundles over $S^4$ and a completely distinguished odd-integer family of non-spin six-manifolds. A doubled-quotient argument excludes the configuration with two boundary fixed points and an interior singular orbit, while the configuration with one fixed point and an exceptional interval has underlying manifold $\mathbb{CP}^3$. For a boundaryless $SU(2)$ quotient, an adjoint-weight matching argument reduces the exceptional three-orbit case to a unique action on the Eschenburg flag and identifies every two-orbit candidate with a weighted action on $S^2\times S^4$. These classifications imply rational ellipticity throughout the stated symmetry class. We also establish restricted curvature obstructions for the two diagonal product actions, without asserting nonexistence for arbitrary invariant metrics. Abstract graph restrictions, smooth realizability, and positive-curvature realizability are kept distinct. Some of the results in this paper are discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors.

metadata.title: Boundary of Anosov coaffine representations
metadata.abstract: Let $\Gamma \le \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free hyperbolic group dividing a properly and strictly convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb R\mathrm P^d$, and let $\rho: \Gamma \to \mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb R)$ be the inclusion. We study representations of $\Gamma$ into the coaffine group that are deformations of $\rho\oplus 1 \in \mathrm{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathrm{GL}(d+2,\mathbb R))$ and that lie on the boundary of the locus of projective Anosov representations. In this setting, we identify a canonical limit set $\Lambda$ for the action and study its fine geometric features which are, in a suitable sense, stable. We prove the existence of an ending lamination that encodes the failure of the Anosov condition and the non-existence of a Cannon--Thurston map. Under certain conditions, we compute the Hausdorff dimension and show that the corresponding measure is positive.

metadata.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
metadata.abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.

metadata.title: Anomaly Flow II: Estimates and Long-time Existence for the Coupled Flow
metadata.abstract: In this follow-up to \cite{Sua25}, we extend the results to the coupled anomaly flow which incorporates the evolution of a Hermitian metric on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact complex $3$-fold with general slope parameter $\alpha'$. This yields a similar sufficient smallness condition on the slope parameter $\alpha'$ in order to extend the flow on $[0, \tau)$ to $[0, \tau + \epsilon)$. We also augment the argument of \cite{Sua25} slightly to fix the peculiarity of the units in the condition for $\alpha'$ for the $k = 1$ case.

metadata.title: Strongly isotropy irreducible spaces whose Laplacians have all their eigenspaces irreducible
metadata.abstract: Let $H$ be a closed subgroup of a compact connected Lie group $G$ such that $G/H$ is simply connected, the action of $G$ on $G/H$ is almost effective, and $G/H$ is a strongly isotropy irreducible space. The smallest positive eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator $\Delta$ associated to the standard metric on $G/H$ was recently computed. In this article we obtain a second non-zero eigenvalue of $\Delta$. As a consequence, we prove that all eigenspaces of the Laplacian are irreducible as $G$-modules if and only if $(G,H)$ is a compact symmetric pair of real rank one, or $(G,H)$ is equal to $(\operatorname{G}_2,\operatorname{SU}(3))$ or $(\operatorname{Spin}(7),\operatorname{G}_2)$.

metadata.title: Asymptotics of Random-Lattice Enumeration: Beyond HKZ via Dense Sublattices
metadata.abstract: To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it. For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$. This matches the worst-case enumeration exponent of Hanrot-Stehlé and confirms earlier predictions for the geometry of HKZ bases on random lattices. Searching beyond quasi-HKZ bases, we prove that with high probability, the minimum achievable tree size exponent $c$ over all bases of a random lattice satisfies: \begin{align} 0.1464 \approx \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\leq c<0.1474. \end{align} For the lower bound, we use Kim's mean-value formula for nested chains of primitive sublattices to rule out bases with small prefix determinants. This strengthens the earlier Rankin-based heuristic lower bound exponent $c \geq 1/8$, discussed by Nguyen and Hanrot-Stehlé, and rules out the existence of random-lattice bases with trees as small as predicted by the geometric series assumption. For the upper bound, we show that with high probability a dense primitive half-rank sublattice exists with determinant at most $n^{n/8 + o(n)}$. Combining dual HKZ on this sublattice with HKZ on its quotient gives a basis with $c \leq 1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$. Recursively splitting each half lowers the upper bound below $0.1474$, and under a natural heuristic assumption we prove that the lower bound is tight. analysisBasis.abstract: To bridge the gap between worst-case and heuristic analyses of lattice enumeration, we study the sizes of (unpruned) enumeration trees on $n$-dimensional Haar-random lattices. Writing $n^{cn+o(n)}$ for the tree size at the shortest vector radius, we investigate the asymptotic scaling of $c$, and which bases minimize it. For quasi-HKZ bases, we rigorously analyze the random-lattice HKZ geometry and establish $c=1/(2e)\approx 0.1839$. This matches the worst-case enumeration exponent of Hanrot-Stehlé and confirms earlier predictions for the geometry of HKZ bases on random lattices. Searching beyond quasi-HKZ bases, we prove that with high probability, the minimum achievable tree size exponent $c$ over all bases of a random lattice satisfies: \begin{align} 0.1464 \approx \frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}\leq c<0.1474. \end{align} For the lower bound, we use Kim's mean-value formula for nested chains of primitive sublattices to rule out bases with small prefix determinants. This strengthens the earlier Rankin-based heuristic lower bound exponent $c \geq 1/8$, discussed by Nguyen and Hanrot-Stehlé, and rules out the existence of random-lattice bases with trees as small as predicted by the geometric series assumption. For the upper bound, we show that with high probability a dense primitive half-rank sublattice exists with determinant at most $n^{n/8 + o(n)}$. Combining dual HKZ on this sublattice with HKZ on its quotient gives a basis with $c \leq 1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$. Recursively splitting each half lowers the upper bound below $0.1474$, and under a natural heuristic assumption we prove that the lower bound is tight. Combined with the collision search of Feng-Gao-Liu, our two-block construction gives a polynomial-space algorithm solving the closest vector problem with preprocessing (CVPP) on random lattices in query time $n^{0.0892 n + o(n)}$ for arbitrary targets.

metadata.title: Holomorphic Bisectional Curvature on Total Spaces of Holomorphic Vector Bundles
metadata.abstract: We study complete K$ä$hler metrics with prescribed signs of holomorphic bisectional curvature on total spaces of holomorphic vector bundles over compact complex manifolds. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions in the nonnegative and strictly negative cases, characterized respectively by unitary flatness and Griffiths negativity of the bundle, together with the corresponding curvature conditions on the base. We also obtain a global metric splitting in the nonnegative case, rule out strictly positive curvature over positive-dimensional bases, and construct counterexamples to the converse in the nonpositive case.

metadata.title: On the Structure of the Cut Locus in Certain Classes of Warped Product Manifolds
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we determine the structure of the cut locus for a class of complete warped product manifolds $M=(R^1\times S^1,dt^2+m(t)^2d\theta^2)$, where the warping function $m(t)$ is positive and even, under the assumption that there exists a positive number $t_1$ such that the Gaussian curvature is nonpositive on the domain $t^{-1}\left((t_1,\infty) \right)$ and is decreasing along the subarc $t^{-1}([0,t_1])\cap\theta^{-1}(0)$ of the upper half meridian.

metadata.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed axisymmetric hypersurfaces
metadata.abstract: We establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed, embedded, axisymmetric hypersurfaces Sigma in n+1 dimensional Euclidean space R^{n+1}, the dimension n > or = 2, with admissible C^{1,1} profiles. Let H_j be the j-th normalized mean curvature. If Sigma is axiconvex, i.e., every hyperplane orthogonal to the symmetry axis meets the enclosed domain in an n-dimensional ball or empty, then \[\left(\frac{\int_\Sigma H_\ell\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-\ell)} \le \left(\frac{\int_\Sigma H_k\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-k)}, \qquad 0\le\ell<k\le n-1. \] Without axiconvexity, the inequalities hold for sign-corrected integrals \[\int_\Sigma\varepsilon_\theta^{\,j}H_j\,dA,\] where varepsilon_{theta}= {sgn}(sin {theta}) denotes the sign of the azimuthal principal curvatures. As applications, the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities remain valid whenever both l and k are even. Equality in each of the above inequalities holds if and only if Sigma is a round sphere. The proof adapts the rearrangement and tangent angle folding approach of Dalphin-Henrot-Masnou-Takahashi from surfaces of revolution in R^3 to n-dimensional axisymmetric hypersurfaces in R^{n+1}. The higher-dimensional construction uses weighted monotone rearrangement to produce convex comparison bodies with C^{1,1} boundaries.

metadata.title: One boundary, infinitely geometries
metadata.abstract: Let $N$ be a 3-dimensional integral homology sphere. We prove the existence of a sequence of 4-dimensional topologically negatively curved manifolds $M_k$, $k=1,2,\dots$, satisfying the following: (1) all aspherical manifolds $M_k$ have the same universal cover $U_N$ depending only on $N$; (2) all fundamental groups $\pi_1(M_k)$ are hyperbolic and share the same Gromov boundary $X_N$ depending only on $N$; (3) the groups $\pi_1(M_k)$ represent infinitely many distinct quasi-isometry classes. The last conclusion, which represents the new feature, shows that negatively curved geometries in dimension 4 exhibit substantially richer structure than those in dimension 3.

metadata.title: Every n points in the plane contain (m1 + o(1)) n points with no unit distance
metadata.abstract: Let $f(n)$ be the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $f(n)$ points no two at distance $1$, and let $m_1$ be the supremum of the upper densities of Lebesgue measurable planar sets with no two points at distance $1$. Larman and Rogers observed that $f(n) \ge m_1 n$. We prove that $f(n)/n \to m_1$; that is, $f(n) = (m_1 + o(1))n$. This is the first half of a conjecture of Dúcz and Varga, and with the bound $m_1 \le 0.247$ of Ambrus, Csiszárik, Matolcsi, Varga and Zsámboki it gives $f(n) \le (0.247 + o(1))n$. The proof builds a random independent subset of the algebraic plane, invariant under algebraic translations and rotations, whose probability of containing the origin is at least the worst finite independence ratio, and turns it into a measurable planar set of at least that upper density. Its only non-classical input is the Haar rigidity theorem for wild character laws from the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable, which has a machine-checked Lean proof. The whole argument has been formalized in Lean 4 on top of it.

metadata.title: Spectral Gårding Elliptic Equations
metadata.abstract: We study spectral Gårding elliptic equations on compact Kähler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal Gårding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Székelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact Kähler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal Gårding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.

metadata.title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
metadata.abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.

analysis.workSummary: 在环境维数不超过七时，证明 Almgren–Taylor–Wang 与 Luckhaus–Sturzenhecker 最小化移动格式的 varifold 极限为整 Brakke 流，其 L¹ 极限即平坦流为广义 BV 流。结果不要求能量收敛，且允许增厚现象。
analysis.breakthrough: 在缺少能量收敛时仍把离散变分极限统一到 Brakke 与 BV 弱流框架。
analysis.limitations: 环境维数限制为至多七；增厚存在时结论仍是弱流结构。
analysis.priorityReason: 平均曲率弱流之间关系的关键无附加能量收敛结果。

analysisBasis.abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.

metadata.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
metadata.abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

analysis.limitations: 作用针对有理点群与球面；不延拓指实 Lie 群连续作用，而非每个作用映射不连续。
analysis.priorityReason: 群作用刚性边界及球面动力系统的构造。

metadata.title: Symplectic four-manifolds and hyperbolic $π$-orbifolds
metadata.abstract: We construct closed symplectic 4-manifolds admitting the structure of hyperbolic $\pi$-orbifold, addressing LeBrun's conjecture. Our simplest example has Euler characteristic $304$, is tessellated by $64$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic $120$-cell and admits a four-fold branched covering over a product of two surfaces of genus $4$.

metadata.title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for Rényi Entropy
metadata.abstract: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for Rényi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.

analysis.topic: 度量测度几何、极限与奇异空间
analysis.progressType: Rényi 熵尖锐 Rogers–Shephard 界
analysis.workSummary: 对对数凹随机向量的独立同分布副本 X、X′，建立 p≥1 与 a,b>0 下 hₚ(aX−bX′)≤hₚ(X)+n log(a+b)，并给出各端点等号分类。作者宣称 Shannon 情形解决 Madiman–Kontoyiannis 的熵 Rogers–Shephard 猜想，同时用高维单纯形证明 0<p<1 时非加权界可失效。

analysis.limitations: 要求对数凹分布及独立同分布副本；p=∞ 的等号类比有限 p 更大，p<1 不可推广同一界。
analysis.priorityReason: 凸几何与信息熵之间的重要尖锐不等式及猜想主张。

metadata.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
metadata.abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.

analysis.topic: 几何分析、几何 PDE 与几何流
analysis.progressType: 不交极小图猜想的必要性质
analysis.workSummary: 设三个互不相交的单连通平面无界域上存在正值、边界为零的极小图，正文定理1证明每个图的圆周最大高度M(r,u)在大r时被正常数倍r上下夹住。以半平面等温坐标写成单叶调和映射h+ḡ，并归一化高度为2Re ζ、g′=−1/h′；定理2给指定子扇形像域中的Laplacian按1/|z|衰减及接近极限扇形边界的次线性高度。

metadata.title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
metadata.abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le \alpha<1$, we show the existence of a $C^{1,\alpha}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. We show that in step-2 Carnot groups the construction gives hypersurfaces of maximal Euclidean Hausdorff dimension, equal to $q-\frac{1+\alpha}{2}$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. Here the range of unrectifiability is sharp, since for $\alpha=1$ the surface is rectifiable in the classical sense. In step-2 Carnot groups, it is also possible to prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. These results extend the seminal work by Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group.

analysis.progressType: Carnot 曲面的不可整流构造
analysis.workSummary: 在任意非交换 Carnot 群中，对 0≤α<1 构造内蕴 C¹,α_H 正则、但欧氏 Hausdorff 维数大于拓扑维数的曲面。二步群中超曲面的欧氏维数达到 q−(1+α)/2，而 α=1 时恢复经典可整流性；同时证明 C¹_H 超曲面的 q−1/2 维欧氏 Hausdorff 测度为零。
analysis.breakthrough: 把内蕴正则与欧氏不可整流性的尖锐反差推广到一般非交换群。
analysis.limitations: 最大维数公式与测度零结果针对二步群；α=1 不属于不可整流区间。
analysis.priorityReason: 次黎曼正则性与欧氏测度几何之间的尖锐界线。

metadata.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
metadata.abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of Kähler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform à priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.

analysis.topic: 几何分析、几何 PDE 与几何流
analysis.progressType: 退化 Kähler 类的辅助 Hessian 方程
analysis.workSummary: 在紧Kähler n维流形上取半正定χ，其nef类的数值维数k=n−1，令ω_t=χ+tω_X。对右端密度一致Lq控制、q>2的归一化退化k-Hessian方程，正文定理3给出独立于t的L∞估计；定理6对相应退化线性化算子的零均值v、指定超水平集上的二次可微与L v≥−a条件，给出sup v≤C(1+L¹范数)的平均值界。
analysis.breakthrough: 以数值维数对应的混合体积替代必须big的顶次体积，在k=n−1的非big退化中获得统一估计。

metadata.title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
metadata.abstract: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fréchet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.
metadata.comment: 20 pages; 4 appendices; one synthetic experiment included

metadata.title: Sharp stability for mixed bubbles on hyperbolic space
metadata.abstract: We prove sharp residual stability estimates for the critical Poincaré-Sobolev equation near sums of one positive hyperbolic solution and one projected Euclidean bubble in dimensions at least four. The estimates are uniform in the relative positions of the centers. The sharp rate is linear except in dimension six, where it contains a square root of a logarithm. For nonnegative functions, the same estimates hold under an energy constraint near the sum of the two profile energies for \(\lambda\) outside a finite set, and an additional mass constraint removes this restriction. For arbitrary finite numbers of profiles, we identify and realize all nonnegative Palais-Smale levels. We characterize the parameters at which different pairs of profile numbers have the same energy and show that the limiting energy and mass determine both profile numbers.

metadata.title: The inf spectrum of moduli space
metadata.abstract: Given a surface of genus $g \geq 2$, its inf spectrum is the ordered multiset of inf lengths of curves on the surface, the infimum being over all hyperbolic metrics. We show that the inf spectrum has exponential growth with coefficients that only depend on g, improving the earlier double exponential upper bound. The proof involves developing a number of tools including the process of "thickening" a surface and the notion of model surfaces. These tools may be of independent interest.

metadata.title: Regularity theorems for Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system
metadata.abstract: We prove several regularity theorems concerning Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system. The main lemma (i.e. ``Decoupling Lemma") says that the component functions of such solutions satisfy the homogeneous Pucci inequalities. This allows us to apply the regularity theory for scalar viscosity solutions for elliptic PDE component-wise to a viscosity solution for the system. As a result of the Decoupling Lemma, we deduce that 2D Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the system are analytic in the interior, and obtain a quantitative partial regularity theorem. We also prove a geometric Harnack inequality for Lipschitz solutions. The Harnack inequality yields a strong maximum principle and half-space Liouville theorem. Another significant consequence of the lemma is a boundary regularity theorem for Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Notably, our theorem does not require any density assumption at the graph boundary, and we do not assume stationarity. This is used to prove a classification theorem for the singular set of a 4D stationary solution on a bounded domain. We also prove an $\varepsilon$-regularity theorem extending a result of the author. To conclude, we survey open problems. As an example, we have included a Bernstein-type theorem for 3D homogeneous entire Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Taken together, our results suggest that viscosity methods are a useful tool for studying the regularity of minimal graphs.

metadata.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
metadata.abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.

analysis.topic: 曲率与比较几何
analysis.progressType: 积分 Menger 曲率圆周极小性
analysis.workSummary: 证明任意 p≥2 时，固定长度的闭嵌入 C¹ 曲线中圆周唯一极小化积分 Menger 曲率。p>3 时借助自避与正则性可推广到像集长度给定的闭可求长曲线，并得到识别平凡结的性质。
analysis.breakthrough: 给出所有 p≥2 的尖锐下界和唯一圆周等号结构。

analysisBasis.abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.

metadata.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
metadata.abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

metadata.title: Loop Fundamental Quandles: A Geometric Generalization of the Knot Quandle
metadata.abstract: The knot quandle, introduced independently by Joyce and Matveev, admits a geometric description in terms of nooses. Motivated by this description, we introduce the \textit{loop fundamental quandle} $LQ(X,A,\ast)$ of a pair $(X,A)$ with a fixed base point $\ast\in X$. Its elements are represented by pairs consisting of a loop in $A$ and a path joining the base point of the loop to the fixed base point $\ast$. More generally, for a loop condition $P$ on $A$, invariant under free homotopy, we define the loop fundamental quandle $LQ(X,A,\ast;P)$. We establish functoriality and homotopy invariance of the loop fundamental quandle and show that it admits a natural augmented quandle structure over $\pi_1(X,\ast)$. For a knot $K$ in $S^3$, applying the construction to its exterior gives the \textit{knot loop quandle} $LQ(K,\ast;P)$. Appropriate choices of the loop condition recover the knot quandle, its $n$-th power quandles, and the full knot quandle. The construction is inspired by Joyce's noose-theoretic approach, but allows loop data that need not arise as the boundary of a disk satisfying the noose condition.

metadata.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
metadata.abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.

metadata.title: A Dimension Estimate for Polynomial Growth Holomorphic Functions
metadata.abstract: On a complete noncompact Kähler manifold $M^n$ of complex dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature, we prove that polynomial growth holomorphic functions of degree $d$ ($d\geq 0$) have an dimension upper bound $C(n)(1+d)^n$. In particular, $\dim_{\C}\OO_d(M)\leq C'(n)d^n,$ for $d\geq1$, and the estimate is sharp.

metadata.title: Higher order isoperimetric inequalities and rigidity for surfaces in $\R^n$
metadata.abstract: We establish a family of sharp higher order isoperimetric type inequalities for smooth compact surfaces in Euclidean spaces of arbitrary codimension. These inequalities involve arbitrarily high derivatives of the boundary curve, together with the mean curvature vector of the surface. For example, the first and second order inequalities yield the sharp two-sided estimate for the isoperimetric deficit: \begin{align*} & \frac{\pi}{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-R\nu|^2\, ds +2\pi\int_M x\cdot H\, dA \le L^2-4\pi A\\ \le& \frac{\pi}{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-R\nu|^2\, ds +2\pi\int_M x\cdot H\, dA +\frac{\pi}{3R}\int_{\partial M}|x+R^2\kappa|^2\, ds, \end{align*} where $R=\frac{L}{2\pi}$ and the origin is chosen to be the centroid of the boundary. For minimal surfaces, equality in the lower bound holds precisely for flat disks, whereas the second inequality admits non-round equality cases. Our results extend that of Carleman, Sachs, Chakerian, and Li-Schoen-Yau. A distinctive feature of our work is the unexpected rigidity structure arising at higher orders. At the first and second orders, equality curves admit decompositions into circular Fourier modes supported in mutually orthogonal planes. Remarkably, this phenomenon fails at higher orders. We establish a multiplicative factorization of the unit tangent map into elementary planar rotations acting on a fixed unit vector, providing a characterization of equality cases at arbitrary order. As a result, we construct a third order equality curve in $\mathbb R^3$ whose Fourier modes cannot be decomposed into mutually orthogonal circular modes.

metadata.title: Optimal Synthesis on the Special Linear Group
metadata.abstract: We study the exponential map on the group of real two-by-two matrices with determinant one, endowed with a left-invariant Riemannian metric. Using the Euler-Poincaré equation and its linearization, we determine the conjugate and Maxwell times and identify a domain on which the exponential map is a global diffeomorphism onto the complement of the Maxwell stratum. This provides an alternative proof that the first Maxwell time coincides with the cut time. We obtain an explicit matrix description of the cut locus and characterize the globally minimizing geodesics. Furthermore, we analyze the first Maxwell-time function, determine its unique global minimum, and show that the injectivity radius is $\frac{\pi \sqrt{14}}{4}$. Finally, we characterize the intersection of the cut and conjugate loci and prove that every geodesic is equi-optimal.

metadata.title: Four-dimensional almost-Einstein manifolds with circulant structures
metadata.abstract: This paper considers a four-dimensional Riemannian manifold with an additional circulant tensor structure $Q$. We prove that such a manifold is almost-Einstein if the curvature tensor preserves the action of the structure on the last two arguments. Additionally, we examine an associated Riemannian product manifold $(M, g, Q)$ where $P=Q^{2}$, deriving explicit expressions for the curvature tensor in terms of the metric and the product structure. The sectional and Ricci curvatures of these manifolds are determined using special bases generated by the images of a given vector under the structure $Q$. Finally, we construct a non-trivial example of a four-dimensional locally product manifold by embedding a four-dimensional hypersurface into a ten-dimensional Euclidean space.

metadata.title: Biconservative hypersurfaces in Euclidean Spaces
metadata.abstract: An isometric immersion $X: \Sigma^n \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is biharmonic (BHH) if $\Delta^2 X = 0$, i.e., if $\Delta H =0$, where $\Delta$ and $H$ are the metric Laplacian and the mean curvature vector field of $\Sigma^n$ respectively. More generally, biconservative hypersurfaces (BCHs) are isometric immersions for which only the tangential part of the biharmonic equation vanishes. BCHs are first described and then constructed.

analysisBasis.abstract: An isometric immersion $X: \Sigma^n \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is biharmonic (BHH) if $\Delta^2 X = 0$, i.e., if $\Delta H =0$, where $\Delta$ and $H$ are the metric Laplacian and the mean curvature vector field of $\Sigma^n$ respectively. More generally, biconservative hypersurfaces (BCHs) are isometric immersions for which only the tangential part of the biharmonic equation vanishes. BCHs are first described and then constructed.

metadata.title: On the Weyl tube formula for nonlocal perimeters
metadata.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the nonlocal perimeter of tubular neighbourhoods. For a closed $C^{1,1}$ submanifold of Euclidean space, we show that a suitable rescaling of the nonlocal perimeter of its tube converges to an explicit constant times the Hausdorff measure of the submanifold. The constant is the fractional perimeter of the unit ball in the codimension of the submanifold. For finite point sets, we obtain an exact tube formula in terms of a generalised hypergeometric function. In contrast with the classical Weyl formula, this expansion has infinitely many terms, contains both noninteger and integer powers of the tubular radius, and has coefficients that depend on the relative positions of the points rather than only on their intrinsic geometry. We also establish a point-set expansion for general analytic kernels.

metadata.title: The triangular metric on projective surfaces
metadata.abstract: In \cite{ThurstonStretch} Thurston introduced stretch paths and stretch maps between hyperbolic surfaces. In this paper we extend similar constructions to the space of convex real projective structures on surfaces. Using Fock-Goncharov-like parameters, we introduce stretch paths and construct explicit stretch maps between the projective surface. We show that stretch maps are $e^t$--Lipschitz with respect to a triangular metric we introduce on the projective surface. This allows us to gain control on several length functions on an open set of the space of convex real projective structures (those where there is no ``local back--tracking"). As an application we obtain pointwise upper bounds for the Hilbert entropy of some convex real projective structures in terms of Fock-Goncharov-like parameters.
