metadata.title: An Algebraic Matching Algorithm for the Genus of Grid Diagrams
metadata.abstract: Grid diagrams encode knots and links combinatorially through an (n,n) winding matrix W(G). A fundamental invariant of the grid diagram is its genus g(G), which records essential topological information about the underlying knot. We give an algebraic algorithm that computes g(G) directly from W(G). The method repurposes the Hungarian algorithm ,after a column normalization that makes the matrix non-negative, it applies row-column reductions and minimum-vertex-cover corrections until the zero entries admit a perfect matching, equivalently until the minimum marking number equals n. By Konig's theorem the resulting permutation defines a distinguished grid state, and g(G) is then read from this matrix via the classical grid homology formula (Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo). The novelty of this paper is the algorithm and its strongly polynomial analysis; the underlying invariant is known grid-homology theory. We illustrate the method on the trefoil and additional examples, and discuss extensions to (m,n) matrices and grid-move navigation toward the knot genus g(K).

metadata.title: Knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
metadata.abstract: We determine the Maslov-graded next-to-top term of knot Floer homology for fibered positive links. Its rank in Maslov grading (-1) is the number of nontrivial prime connected-sum factors plus the number of components minus one, and the remaining summand is supported in Maslov grading zero. For a knot, the dimension of this remaining summand is determined by its Alexander polynomial. The proof combines a preferred-crossing construction with reductions of generalized Seifert surfaces to planar pretzel surfaces and a graded skein induction. We also obtain bounds on the fixed points of monodromies for fibered positive knots.

metadata.title: Ricci pinching on complete Kahler manifolds
metadata.abstract: We study Ricci pinching problem on complete Kähler manifolds. For complete noncompact manifolds with Euclidean volume growth, we prove flatness under nonnegative bisectional curvature and Ricci pinching, and Ricci flatness under nonnegative Ricci curvature, quadratic curvature decay, and the same pinching condition. In both cases, the pinching constant may tend to zero at a logarithmic rate. Examples show that the logarithmic exponent is sharp in complex dimension two. Second part of the paper proves that a complete Kähler manifold of complex dimension at least two with positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is compact if its sectional curvature is nonnegative and its Ricci curvature is uniformly pinched outside a compact set. No volume-growth assumption or curvature upper bound is needed. Heat smoothing of the Busemann function supplies a strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion with bounded gradient, so the general top Ricci-mass theorem of Datar--Pingali--Seshadri applies. The new ingridents are integral estimates for the Ricci form. The analytic arguments use scalar curvature gap theorems and a critical-$L^n$ vanishing theorem for closed real $(1,1)$-forms under nonnegative Ricci curvature and nonnegative quadratic orthogonal bisectional curvature. The Hodge-Laplace heat eqution deformation conserves the signed top-degree integral, including its initial value, while norm domination and scalar heat-semigroup decay force this integral to vanish. For semipositive initial forms this gives pointwise vanishing of the top wedge power.

metadata.title: Minimal time for heat observability on almost-Riemannian surfaces
metadata.abstract: We determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-Riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple Baouendi-Grushin circles. The structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. The formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. Regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. For singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. We also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. Their superpositions give a lower bound for the Schrödinger observation time.

metadata.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
metadata.abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and Şavk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite, the symmetries of a knot with a prime, reduced alternating diagram without non-trivial flypes are the symmetries of the diagram (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and we show that the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.

metadata.title: Homotopy Self-Equivalences of $\mathbb{R}P^2\times S^2$ and a Braid for non-orientable $4$-Manifolds
metadata.abstract: We compute the group of based homotopy classes of self-homotopy equivalences of the non-orientable $4$-manifold $\RP^2\times S^2$. It is an elementary abelian $2$-group of rank $5$. The subgroup of classes whose based lift to the universal cover $S^2\times S^2$ has degree $+1$ has rank $4$ and is isomorphic to the group of free homotopy classes. The group maps onto the group of self-equivalences of the algebraic $2$-type, which has order $8$, with kernel $\pi_4(\RP^2\times S^2)\cong(\Z/2)^2$ generated by pinch-fold maps; that these maps are independent is shown by an adjunction argument. We then construct a non-orientable analogue of the Hambleton--Kreck braid of exact sequences in dimension $4$, for non-orientable manifolds with spin universal cover, stated for finite fundamental group. We apply the braid to $\RP^2\times S^2$ and to $\RP^4$, and for the Hambleton--Hillman manifold with fundamental group $(\Z/2)^2$ we determine the normal $1$-type and show that self-equivalences act on $\pi_2$ through diagonal sign matrices. For $\RP^2\times S^2$ the pinch-fold maps are detected by twisted spin bordism, and, assuming facts from surgery theory stated as hypotheses, exactly one of the three non-trivial pinch-fold maps is homotopic to a homeomorphism.

metadata.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
metadata.abstract: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_\theta$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

metadata.title: Sharp parameter gaps for quantized Mabuchi energies and cscK metrics
metadata.abstract: For polarized manifolds, we show that semistability for the quantized Mabuchi energy at one fixed finite parameter is equivalent to uniform K-stability and to unique existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler (cscK) metrics. We obtain sharp comparisons between quantized Mabuchi slopes at different parameters and with the ordinary Mabuchi slope. In the presence of automorphisms, we give an equivariant criterion using torus twists under the vanishing of the Futaki character. The estimates also hold for finite-energy geodesic rays in compact Kähler classes. On a fixed ruled surface with discrete automorphism group, we construct cscK polarizations with unbounded critical parameters. Their ratios to the $\alpha$-invariant are also unbounded.

metadata.title: On Intersection of Character Varieties Associated to Dehn Fillings of the Whitehead Link and Its Generalization
metadata.abstract: The canonical component of the character variety of a hyperbolic 2-bridge link complement M is an algebraic surface, from the work of Thurston. If we fix a boundary component T of M and perform a Dehn-filling on T, we get a 1-cusped manifold whose character variety is commonly a generalized curve that is naturally embedded in the character variety of M. If we perform distinct Dehn-fillings on M, we get various generalized curves on the canonical surface. In this paper, we analyze how these curves intersect with each other in the surface and study the topological implications for these intersection points. We also classify the intersection points that correspond to reducible characters, using the twisted Alexander polynomials associated to the Dehn-fillings. Throughout the paper, we use the Whitehead link as a motivating example to illustrate our core methodology, while some generalizations to other 2-bridge links will also be discussed.

metadata.title: Revisiting the Bobkov-Chistyakov-Götze theorem on approximately Gaussian marginals
metadata.abstract: We study one-dimensional marginals of an isotropic, log-concave probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We show that the Kolmogorov distance between a typical marginal and the standard Gaussian distribution is at most $C/n$, for a universal constant $C > 0$. This bound is optimal in general, up to the value of the universal constant. It improves the Gaussian approximation bound of Bobkov, Chistyakov and Götze by a logarithmic factor in the log-concave setting.

metadata.title: Essential factors for surface homeomorphisms
metadata.abstract: Let $f$ be a homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least one that is isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism, possibly relative to a finite invariant set. We construct an intrinsic monotone factor by collapsing the maximal continua whose iterates have uniformly bounded diameter in the universal cover. The quotient is homeomorphic to the original surface and the factor is isotopic to $f$ and has several strongly chaotic dynamical features. It is infinitely continuum-wise expansive, tight, and topologically mixing, and it has a dense family of rotational horseshoes, dense periodic points, and a single topological homoclinic class. The factor can be taken as an area-preserving homeomorphism. The quotient preserves stable translation length on the fine curve graph and the applicable homological rotation sets. When $f$ is $C^\infty$, a companion paper gives a unique measure of maximal entropy for the factor; it has full support and is Bernoulli.

metadata.title: Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in complex space forms
metadata.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surface of constant Gaussian curvature $K$ in a two-dimensional complex space form $\Mtilde^2(4\epsilon)$ of constant holomorphic sectional curvature $4\epsilon$, and let $H$ denote its mean curvature vector field. We prove that either $K=\epsilon$ or $K=0\ne\epsilon$ and $|H|$ is constant. In particular, if $|H|$ is non-constant, then $K=\epsilon$.

metadata.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
metadata.abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $\sigma : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $\Lambda$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in \Lambda} \|\sigma_i -\sigma_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $\sigma_{|\partial \Lambda}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main Hölder regularity statement in a large domain $\Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $\sigma$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the Hölder regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $\sigma \in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial \Lambda}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.

metadata.title: Non-algebraicity of the Lawson surfaces $ξ_{k,l}$
metadata.abstract: We prove that every Lawson surface $\xi_{k,l}\subset\mathbb S^3$ of genus $kl>1$ is non-algebraic: any real polynomial vanishing on $\xi_{k,l}$ vanishes identically on $\mathbb S^3$. This answers a question posed by Hsiang in 1967 and proves Lawson's 1970 conjecture for $\xi_{2,2}$. The proof uses a reflection principle for the monodromy of the associated family of flat connections.

metadata.title: Morita Invariance of Saturated and Split Subgroupoids for Orbifold Embeddings
metadata.abstract: Borzellino and Brunsden introduced a general notion of suborbifold and proved that a suborbifold is the image of a complete orbifold embedding if and only if it is both saturated and split. Their definitions and proofs are formulated in the classical language of orbifold charts. In this paper we translate these notions into the language of proper étale Lie this http URL introduce the groupoid analogues of saturation and splitting, which we call \emph{orbit saturation} and \emph{stabilizer splitting}, and prove that they coincide with the chart-based conditions. Our main theorem states that a subgroupoid is the image of a complete orbifold embedding if and only if it is both orbit saturated and stabilizer split. We then prove that these notions are Morita invariant: if two orbifold groupoids are Morita equivalent, then their orbit saturated and stabilizer split subgroupoids correspond naturally to each other. This solves an open problem raised by Mestre and Weilandt and explains why the embedding definition of Cho--Hong--Shin fails to be Morita invariant. Along the way we provide detailed examples, including the diagonal embedding, the non-split example of Borzellino and Brunsden, and explicit Morita equivalences.

metadata.title: Exponential profiles for the intrinsic volumes of Orlicz balls
metadata.abstract: An Orlicz ball is the set of points where the sum of a fixed even convex function of the coordinates does not exceed a given radius, here proportional to the dimension. For a broad class of such functions, including non-homogeneous ones, we find the exponential rate of the intrinsic volumes whose order is proportional to the dimension and express it by a two-parameter variational formula involving only one-dimensional integrals. As a function of the order-to-dimension ratio, this rate is concave and continuous on the closed unit interval, and the convergence is uniform in the order. This proves the exponential-profile conjecture of Kabluchko, Marynych, and Prochno for these bodies and recovers their result for $\ell_p$ balls with $p>1$. The proof relies on the theory of large deviations. An exact formula for the Laplace transform of the intrinsic volumes in the radius, extending theirs for $\ell_p$ balls, plays the role of a moment generating function, and a Laplace method gives its exponential rate. An exponential change of measure, analogous to that used in Cramér's theorem, then recovers the intrinsic volumes. The key step is a lower bound on the tilted density at its mean, obtained from log-concavity rather than a law of large numbers.

metadata.title: The Adiabatic b-Calculus and the Global Anomaly Formula on Manifolds with Boundary
metadata.abstract: We study the determinant line bundle for a family of elliptic operators on compact manifolds with boundary with the associated Quillen metric and Bismut-Freed connection, and we prove the global anomaly formula in this context. This extends Witten's holonomy theorem to manifolds with boundary. Witten studied the limiting behavior of the eta invariant of a Dirac operator on the total space of a fibration over $\mathbb{S}^1$ when the metric in the base $\mathbb{S}^1$ is blown up in a certain manner, a process known as taking the adiabatic limit. In this paper, we construct the calculus of adiabatic $b$-pseudodifferential operators, which naturally synthesizes the $b$-calculus and the adiabatic calculus of pseudodifferential operators. Using this calculus, and assuming the fiber operators to be invertible, we compute the adiabatic limit of the natural eta invariant in this setting and relate it to the integral of the Bismut-Freed connection and new correction terms coming from the boundary of the fibers.

metadata.title: Spectral and Nodal Properties of Static Manifolds with Boundary
metadata.abstract: We study compact static manifolds with boundary from a spectral point of view, with particular emphasis on the relation between Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin spectra and the nodal structure of static potentials. We establish comparison inequalities linking Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues with the scalar curvature and derive sufficient spectral conditions ensuring that a static potential changes sign. We also obtain bounds on the number of connected components of the zero set, sufficient conditions for its connectedness, and sufficient conditions ensuring that its components intersect the boundary. Finally, we study variational properties of Robin static triples and characterize compact Robin static triples whose metrics are critical for the first mixed Robin--Dirichlet eigenvalue under admissible volume-preserving deformations.

metadata.title: Intrinsic Geometry Matching: learning observation-equivariant process geometry
metadata.abstract: Real data are often arbitrary, indirect observations of an unknown underlying process, and those observations can distort its geometry. Existing geometric methods equip data with the induced geometry of the ambient space, but this entangles the true geometry of the process with the distortion of the observation. To address this, we introduce Intrinsic Geometry Matching (IGM): a scalable approach to learn the intrinsic geometry of the underlying process. Specifically, we learn the carré du champ operator of the process, allowing us to recover its diffusion geometry. Our method uses the fact that data often come with natural perturbations, like steps in a time series, to recover the intrinsic carré du champ while transforming naturally with changes in observation: it is observation-equivariant. Furthermore, since this equivariance relates the geometry of different spaces, we can train a model using additional sources of data, even when that data lies in another space. We evaluate IGM on molecular dynamics, image, and video data and find better performance and scaling than existing neural and graph-based geometric tools.

metadata.title: A new family of constant width bodies obtained from Reuleaux polyhedra
metadata.abstract: We give a construction of a body of constant width from a unit Reuleaux polyhedron that preserves all its symmetries. As opposed to the Meissner surgery, our construction modifies both edges of each dual pair and requires no choice between them. For the Reuleaux tetrahedron it recovers a previously known body of constant width with six elliptic edges and tetrahedral symmetry.

metadata.title: Intrinsic Rigidity of Bar-and-Joint Frameworks on Riemannian Manifolds
metadata.abstract: We develop an intrinsic rigidity theory for bar-and-joint frameworks whose vertices are constrained to a Riemannian manifold and whose edges are given by minimizing geodesic arcs. Such frameworks are called rigid if they cannot be deformed beyond the ambient isometries, while preserving the geodesic edge lengths. For admissible placements, for which adjacent vertices are joined by unique minimizing geodesics, we define a coordinate-free rigidity operator as the differential of the squared geodesic distance of the edges. By the first-variation formula, its edge rows are expressed in terms of the Riemannian logarithm, providing an intrinsic analogue of the classical Euclidean rigidity matrix. Trivial motions are characterized by orbits of the diagonal action of the isometry group, leading to notions of infinitesimal and local rigidity. We further develop a covariant second-order rigidity theory using the Riemannian Hessians of the edge constraints and characterize second-order rigidity through self-stresses and associated quadratic forms. Finally, we show that infinitesimal and second-order rigidity can be used as sufficient conditions for the local rigidity of an intrinsic framework. Our overarching goal is to provide a unified differential-geometric formulation of intrinsic framework rigidity on smooth manifolds.

metadata.title: Identifiability and Consistent Recovery for the Unnormalized Graph Laplace Operators
metadata.abstract: We study whether an unnormalized graph Laplace operator can determine both the geometry of a manifold and its sampling density. On a fixed compact smooth manifold without boundary, we use a known positive, continuous, strictly decreasing radial kernel at a fixed positive bandwidth. For positive sampling densities, the operator built from geodesic distances determines the Riemannian metric and identifies the density up to equality almost everywhere. When the metric is induced by a Euclidean embedding, the operator built from ambient distances also determines the embedding up to rotations, reflections and translations, and the density. On compact parameter classes with positive continuous densities, minimizing the distance between empirical and popula- tion operators gives estimates that converge to the true parameters under independent, identically distributed sampling. This recovery result assumes that the empirical operator can be evaluated at arbitrary points of the manifold.

metadata.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
metadata.abstract: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Frączyk, Mellick, and Wilkens ( arXiv:2307.01194 ) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and Ünel ( arXiv:2303.16831 ). In this paper we introduce and study ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on higher rank symmetric spaces. We show that ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with respect to polyhedral Finsler metrics can exhibit either behavior seen in these previous works: generically they resemble the hyperbolic case, where almost surely all cells have bounded sides. We further introduce the ideal Selberg--Poisson--Voronoi tessellation of the space of positive definite symmetric matrices, which has particularly nice properties.

metadata.title: Absolutely minimising Lipschitz extensions between Hilbert spaces
metadata.abstract: Every Lipschitz map from a closed subset of a real Hilbert space into a real Hilbert space has an absolutely minimising Lipschitz extension: an extension whose Lipschitz constant on every open subset of the complement, bounded or not, equals the Lipschitz constant of its restriction to the boundary of that subset. Neither space need be separable. This answers a question of Naor and Sheffield. For targets of dimension at least two we prove a density theorem on connected domains: every optimal extension of a boundary datum can be approximated, uniformly on compact sets, by extensions whose Lipschitz constant on every nonempty open subset, and on its boundary, equals the constant of the datum. Consequently, in contrast with the scalar case, such a datum has a unique absolutely minimising extension exactly when its optimal extension is unique, and absolutely minimising extensions need not be closed under uniform convergence, even for fixed smooth data on a planar disk. The extensions are built by finite piecewise isometric interpolation: on nested polyhedra with dense union they are piecewise affine and preserve distances in at least two directions on each simplex, a structure described through leaves of 1-Lipschitz maps. The boundary constraints are handled by a midpoint argument for admissible values, and a Kuratowski-Zorn argument removes the separability assumption while preserving previously prescribed values. We also characterise the bounded linear maps that are absolutely minimising extensions of all data determining their operator norm.

analysisBasis.abstract: Every Lipschitz map from a closed subset of a real Hilbert space into a real Hilbert space has an absolutely minimising Lipschitz extension: an extension whose Lipschitz constant on every open subset of the complement, bounded or not, equals the Lipschitz constant of its restriction to the boundary of that subset. Neither space need be separable. This answers a question of Naor and Sheffield. For targets of dimension at least two we prove a density theorem on connected domains: every optimal extension of a boundary datum can be approximated, uniformly on compact sets, by extensions whose Lipschitz constant on every nonempty open subset, and on its boundary, equals the constant of the datum. Consequently, in contrast with the scalar case, such a datum has a unique absolutely minimising extension exactly when its optimal extension is unique, and absolutely minimising extensions need not be closed under uniform convergence, even for fixed smooth data on a planar disk. The extensions are built by finite piecewise isometric interpolation: on nested polyhedra with dense union they are piecewise affine and preserve distances in at least two directions on each simplex, a structure described through leaves of 1-Lipschitz maps. The boundary constraints are handled by a midpoint argument for admissible values, and a Kuratowski-Zorn argument removes the separability assumption while preserving previously prescribed values. We also characterise the bounded linear maps that are absolutely minimising extensions of all data determining their operator norm.

metadata.title: On the collapsing of spaces with local rewinding Reifenberg control
metadata.abstract: Let $(M^n,g_0)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with $\Ric_{g_0}\ge-(n-1)g_0$ whose local universal covers are uniformly $\delta$-Reifenberg-close to $\R^n$ below a fixed radius $\rho$. We show that for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ there are $\delta(n,\alpha)>0$ and $T(n,\rho,\alpha)>0$ such that, if $\delta\le\delta(n,\alpha)$, a complete Ricci flow $g(t)$ with $g(0)=g_0$ and $|\Rm_{g(t)}|\le\alpha/t$ exists on $(0,T]$. On closed manifolds this is a uniform lower bound for the lifetime of the Ricci flow; on noncompact manifolds, where the initial curvature may be unbounded, it is an existence theorem, and the flow is unique among complete Ricci flows from $g_0$ with a curvature bound of the form $A/t$. The key step is a finite-buffer comparison of two Ricci flows through the Ricci--harmonic map heat flow, following Lee, which transfers a Type-I curvature bound from a complete selected flow to the incomplete flow lifted to a local cover. Consequently, below a dimensional Reifenberg threshold, collapsing closed manifolds admit singular nilpotent fibrations over their Gromov--Hausdorff limits. The Reifenberg hypothesis cannot be weakened to noncollapsing of the local covers: products of shrinking circles with Nifa's four-manifolds have $\Ric\ge0$ and uniformly noncollapsed local covers, but admit no continuous Gromov--Hausdorff approximations onto their limit.

metadata.title: Turaev cobracket, synthetic geometry and applications
metadata.abstract: A teardrop geodesic on a hyperbolic surface is a closed curve that is geodesic except at exactly one point, called its vertex. One imagines a closed curve with one point held down as it deforms to a geodesic. For each teardrop geodesic, we give an explicit geometric construction of the closed geodesic in its free homotopy class. This construction also yields a relation between the length of the teardrop geodesic, the angle at its vertex, and the length of its geodesic representative. We then apply the construction to a self-intersecting closed geodesic at a chosen self-intersection point. Since, at that point, the geodesic splits into two directed teardrop geodesics, our construction gives a geometric description of Turaev's cobracket in terms of geodesic representatives. Using this description we prove that if two self-intersection points yield a pair of canceling terms in the cobracket, then the angle at these points and the lengths of the small loops determined are the same.

metadata.title: Integer decomposition property of three-dimensional smooth polytopes: a shorter proof

metadata.title: Point Processes and Gap Statistics for Translation Surfaces
metadata.abstract: We study the behavior of saddle connection directions on translation surfaces from the point process viewpoint. We define a direction point process for saddle connections of length at most $R>0$ on every translation surface. Given a general ergodic $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$-invariant measure $\mu$ on a stratum of translation surfaces, we also define a slope point process associated with $\mu$. By utilizing the dynamics and geometry of strata, we show that for almost every translation surface, the direction point processes, rescaled by $R^2$, converge in distribution to the slope point process as $R\to\infty$. Using Palm distribution theory, we prove the existence of limiting joint gap distributions and obtain new regularity results for gap distributions associated with the general $\mu$. Finally, we study how these point processes and joint gap distributions behave as the genus $g$ tends to infinity. In the principal stratum, we show that the slope point processes, rescaled by $g^2$, converge in distribution to a Poisson point process. By passing to the corresponding Palm distributions, we show that the rescaled slope gaps converge jointly to independent exponential random variables, which is in stark contrast to the known non-exponential gap distributions in a fixed genus.

metadata.title: Steiner Minimal Trees in the Gromov--Hausdorff Space and in Gromov--Hausdorff Clouds
metadata.abstract: We prove the existence of Steiner minimal trees spanning a finite family of metric spaces in two cases of the Gromov--Hausdorff theory. In the compact Gromov--Hausdorff space $\mathcal{M}$, every finite family of nonempty compact metric spaces is spanned by a shortest Steiner minimal tree whose Steiner vertices are again nonempty compact metric spaces. In a fixed Gromov--Hausdorff cloud $\mathcal{C}$, every finite family of proper, isometrically cobounded spaces admits a finite-length Steiner minimal tree all of whose vertices remain in $\mathcal{C}$. The compact case uses compact replacement through distance profiles and the Hausdorff hyperspace, and the cloud case uses pointed ultralimits.

metadata.title: Purely non-free actions on Riemann surfaces
metadata.abstract: A group of conformal automorphisms of a Riemann surface is said to act purely non-free, or to produce a gpnf-action, if each of its finite-order elements has fixed points. It is known that every finite group admits a gpnf-action on a suitable closed Riemann surface of genus at least two. If $G$ is an infinite countable group, and $X$ is an infinite-type orientable surface, without planar ends and whose space of ends is self-similar, then we observe that there is a Riemann surface structure on $X$ admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. We obtain upper bounds for those finite groups producing a gpnf-action on a closed Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$. If $G$ is a finite group, then its purely non-free genus $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$ is the minimum genus of at least two of a closed Riemann surface admitting a gpnf-action by $G$. This parameter is already known for cyclic, abelian non-cyclic groups, ${\mathcal A}_{4}$, ${\mathcal A}_{5}$ and ${\mathfrak S}_{4}$. For general $G$, we provide the value of $\sigma^{pnf}_{hyp}(G)$, correcting a previous statement on this value. In particular, we observe that every genus is the purely non-free genus of some group. As an application, we describe the minimal purely non-free actions for the family of metacyclic groups $G^{0}_{s}(n)=\langle x,y: x^{n}=y^{2}=1, yxy=x^{s}\rangle,$ where $n \geq 3$ and $2 \leq s \leq n-1$ is such that $s^{2} \equiv 1 \mod(n)$.

metadata.title: Compactness of Cone Yang-Mills Connections
metadata.abstract: We consider the cone Yang-Mills functional recently introduced by Tseng and Zhou. This functional generalizes the Yang-Mills functional by coupling it to a closed 2-form which can represent a geometric structure of interest, e.g. a symplectic form or Ricci form. While the perspective of dimensional reduction is not always possible, we show that a cone Yang-Mills field is always locally the dimensional reduction of a pure Yang-Mills field. We then prove a monotonicity formula and use the dimensional reduction framework to prove an $\epsilon$-regularity theorem in two ways. Finally, we prove a compactness theorem for sequences of cone Yang-Mills connections with bounded action and $L^p$-bounded Higgs fields. Away from a singular set of codimension at least 4 and after suitable bundle identifications, the sequence subconverges in the $C^\infty_{\operatorname{loc}}$-topology.

metadata.title: $3$-manifold groups are linear
metadata.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every compact graph $3$-manifold is linear over the complex numbers. As a corollary, all fundamental groups of compact $3$-manifolds are linear over the complex numbers.

metadata.title: Constant Rank Theorems under Intermediate Ricci Curvature
metadata.abstract: We prove two constant rank theorems for the Ricci tensor in two geometric settings: manifolds with harmonic curvature and gradient Ricci solitons. In both cases, if the $k$-intermediate Ricci curvature satisfies $\Ric_k\geq0$ for some $1\leq k\leq n-2$, then the Ricci tensor has constant rank and its nullity distribution is parallel. In the complete case, the universal cover splits isometrically along the Ricci-null directions. We also show that the range $1\leq k\leq n-2$ is sharp: in every dimension $n\geq4$, nonnegative Ricci curvature alone does not imply the constant rank property in either setting.

metadata.title: Existence and uniqueness of conformal Gauduchon metrics
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we prove that every Hermitian conformal class on a connected noncompact complex manifold of dimension at least two contains a Gauduchon metric. We give a sufficient condition for uniqueness of such Gauduchon metrics up to scaling in terms of functions bounded from above and their Levi forms. This condition is necessary when the manifold has at least two ends. In that case, uniqueness in a fixed conformal class is equivalent to the assertion that every positive solution of the complex Laplace equation for a metric in that class is constant. For a connected noncompact complex Lie group of dimension $n$, uniqueness in every conformal class is equivalent to the assertion that, for every Hermitian metric, every positive solution of the complex Laplace equation is constant. These properties hold exactly when the complex tangent space of a maximal compact subgroup has dimension $n-1$; such a group is abelian. In a conformal class containing a balanced metric, the same equivalence holds without a restriction on the number of ends. We also prove uniqueness for manifolds with a suitable potential on a compactification with compact fibers over a point, the real line, or a parabolic Riemann surface. The examples include compact pluripolar deletions, partially deleted compact fibers, and semipositive line bundles. We construct conformal Gauduchon metrics which are not related by scaling on Stein manifolds and on the total space of $\mathcal O_{\PP^1}(1)^{\oplus2}$.

metadata.title: Non-smooth sub-Riemannian manifolds with non-integer dimension and a Poincaré inequality
metadata.abstract: For every integer $d\geq 3$ and real number $Q\in \left(d,\frac{d(d-1)+2}{2}\right]$, we construct a $Q$-Ahlfors regular metric measure manifold $(M,\mathbf{d},\mu)$ of topological dimension $d$ and analytic dimension $2$ that satisfies a Poincaré inequality. For every $Q>\frac{d(d-1)+2}{2}$, the construction yields a metric measure manifold $(M,\mathbf{d},\mu)$ that is doubling, satisfies a Poincaré inequality, and for which $M$ has $\mu$-essential Hausdorff dimension $Q$. The manifold is $\mathbb{R}^d$ equipped with Lebesgue measure and a sub-Riemannian distance given by vector fields that are locally Hölder continuous but not Lipschitz continuous. These metrics give an uncountable family of new models that are genuinely distinct from the only known families of metric manifolds satisfying a Poincaré inequality: weighted and deformed Carnot groups and smooth sub-Riemannian spaces. The construction is modeled on a singular variant of a filiform Carnot group.

metadata.title: Metaplectic-c prequantizations and the Einstein--Brillouin--Keller quantizability condition
metadata.abstract: We show that every symplectic manifold admits a symplectic form whose metaplectic-c prequantizations give quantizability conditions on all its Lagrangian submanifolds. Metaplectic-c prequantizations descend to prequantizations over the Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle that are fibrewise flat with holonomies primitive fourth roots of unity on the generators of the fundamental groups. This fibrewise holonomy is consistently interpreted as that of both Leray two-orientations and normalized Blattner--Kostant--Sternberg half-forms. The prequantizations pull back to flat circle bundles on each Lagrangian submanifold whose holonomy character defines a quantizability condition. The first and second Stiefel--Whitney classes are identified as splitting obstructions to the Lagrangianwise holonomies. These holonomies split into a product of holonomies on any orientable Lagrangian submanifold, and split consistently for all Lagrangian submanifolds of a manifold with metaplectic structure. When the first Chern class vanishes, the holonomy splits into the Bohr--Sommerfeld factor and a quarter phase Maslov correction, recovering the classical Einstein--Brillouin--Keller condition. We develop the underlying obstruction theory for circle extensions associated to general Lie group double coverings with first hypercohomology groupoids.

metadata.title: Geometry and barycenters in large $\CAT(κ)$ spaces
metadata.abstract: We study the geometry and resulting properties of Fréchet functions and barycenters in metric spaces with curvature bounded above by a positive constant in the sense of Alexandrov. Existing results typically rely on the assumption that the support is small enough that the squared distance, and thus the Fréchet function, is strongly geodesically convex. We work in the sharper regime where existence and uniqueness of the barycenter are guaranteed, but where convexity typically fails. We develop new geometric properties of these spaces, including a quantitative four-point inequality and a geodesic stability result. Using these tools, we establish new finite sample error bounds for two statistical estimators: the empirical barycenter and the iterated barycenter, as well as new results on sparse representations and approximations of barycenters.

metadata.title: A stationary harmonic map with a nonstationary tangent map
metadata.abstract: We construct a stationary weakly harmonic map from a domain in \R^5 into a compact Kähler surface for which a tangent map is weakly harmonic but nonstationary. The target manifold is the blow-up of \CP^1\times\CP^1 at four points lying in one fiber and arranged at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. The nonstationarity of the tangent map arises from the break down of the tetrahedral symmetry in the defect measure concentrated on the vertices.

metadata.title: Equivariant analytic torsion forms
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we first construct infinitesimal equivariant analytic torsion forms for Kähler fibrations. We then compare them with Ma's equivariant analytic torsion forms, modulo $\partial$- and $\overline{\partial}$-exact forms, in terms of equivariant Bott--Chern currents and the $I$-genus. Our comparison formula extends that of Bismut and Goette to families.

metadata.abstract: We prove that the rational Chow ring of every connected component of the multi-scale compactifications of the genus three strata $\mathcal{H}(4), \mathcal{H}(2,2)$ and $\mathcal{H}(3,1)$ is generated by boundary-stratum classes. Our proof shows Chow-Künneth generation property of boundary strata of the multi-scale compactification by reducing the boundary analysis to lower-genus generalized strata of meromorphic differentials, including residueless loci, described through plane-quartic and plane-cubic models. As a consequence, the rational cycle-class map is an isomorphism and the compactifications have no odd rational cohomology.

metadata.title: Tournaments, flags, and spinors
metadata.abstract: It is observed that the dimension of the space of invariant spinors on the manifold $\mathrm{SU}(n)/T^{n-1}$ of full flags in $\mathbb{C}^n$ equals the number $\mathrm{RT}(n)$ of labelled regular tournaments of order $n$, for $n$ odd. This space is decomposed under a double cover of the Weyl group, and realized as a pair of eigenspaces, first for the Dirac operator, then for a twisted version of it which acts equivariantly; this is used to show that multiplicities of irreducible representations are even for $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$.

metadata.title: Excess inertia of finite metric spaces
metadata.abstract: This paper classifies the possible inertias that are realized by an excess matrix of a finite metric space with at most nine points. For the classification, we make use of relationships between finite metric spaces and non-obtuse and acute sets in classical geometry. As an application, we prove that the small-scale limit of the magnitude function of any six-point metric space is at least one whenever this limit exists.

metadata.title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
metadata.abstract: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. metadata.title: Radon Transforms of Projection Functions and Aleksandrov-Fenchel Inequalities
metadata.abstract: The Radon transforms on Grassmannians define two families of geometric operators on convex bodies when applied to their projection functions. On the one hand, these are Minkowski's projection body maps and on the other hand these operators coincide on origin-symmetric bodies with the mean section body maps introduced by Goodey and Weil in 1992. Over the past two decades various sharp isoperimetric inequalities for projection bodies were shown to also hold for mean section bodies. However, an analogue of Lutwak's log-concavity inequalities for the intrinsic volumes of projection bodies remained open for mean section bodies. We establish new Aleksandrov--Fenchel inequalities for averages of certain mixed volumes and apply them to show that also all the intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies are indeed log-concave.

metadata.title: A topological sphere theorem for pinched Legendrian submanifolds
metadata.abstract: Let $M^n$ be a closed simply connected Legendrian submanifold of $\mathbb S^{2n+1}$, where $n\geq5$, and let $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{H}=\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{B}$ denote its second fundamental form and mean-curvature vector. We prove that $M$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb S^n$ if \begin{equation*} |\mathbf{B}|^2\leq \frac{(n-1)(n+2)}n+\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|^2-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|\sqrt{|\mathbf{H}|^2+4n}. \end{equation*} The equality can be attained by the Calabi products, so simple connectivity cannot be omitted. For $n\geq4$, we also prove a sphere theorem under an explicit bound and the weaker assumption $b_1(M;\mathbb R)=0$. The proof combines phase-rotated Lawson--Simons variations with a systolic inequality for finite two-complexes. We also give local constructions showing that the pinching condition allows negative isotropic curvature at a point.

metadata.title: An explicit dimension-free isoperimetric plateau in the cube
metadata.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, the relative Euclidean isoperimetric profile of the unit cube equals one whenever the prescribed volume differs from one half by at most $6.25\times10^{-12}$. The only minimizers in this interval are coordinate slabs. This answers Glaudo's question on the existence of a dimension-free central plateau. The proof combines a dimension-free local optimality estimate for slabs, established through BV slicing and a small-support estimate, with a quantitative Gaussian rigidity argument that forces the normal of an approximating half-space to be close to a coordinate direction.

metadata.title: Pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for complete Ricci flows
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we prove a uniform pseudolocality theorem for smooth complete Ricci flows whose initial metrics have Ricci curvature bounded below and uniformly positive injectivity radius. No a priori curvature bound is assumed on the flow. As a consequence, we obtain strong uniqueness for smooth complete Ricci flows from a complete metric with the above geometric bounds. We also prove that every smooth complete Ricci flow from a complete Ricci-flat metric with uniformly positive injectivity radius is stationary. The same conclusion holds for any complete flat initial metric. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to Chen's question on the strong uniqueness of Ricci flow from Euclidean space in every dimension.

metadata.title: Scalar curvature rigidity of small spherical caps with arbitrary fill-ins
metadata.abstract: We prove an analogue of Min-Oo's conjecture for sufficiently small spherical caps in the unit round sphere. analysisBasis.abstract: We prove an analogue of Min-Oo's conjecture for sufficiently small spherical caps in the unit round sphere. For every dimension $n\ge3$, there exists $r_*(n)>0$ such that the following holds for every round cap of radius $0<r\le r_*(n)$: any smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian fill-in with the same intrinsic boundary metric and with scalar curvature and outward boundary mean curvature at least those of the cap is isometric to the cap.

metadata.title: A parity constraint on the topological numbers of self-complementary triply-periodic surfaces
metadata.abstract: The stability zone of Novikov's problem of planar sections of triply periodic surfaces are labeled by indivisible triples of integers, which we call the soul of the zone. Which triples may occur is not known. We show that, if a Morse function $f$ on $\mathbb T^3$ admits a translation $\tau(x)=x+v$ with $f\circ\tau=-f$, so that the sets $\{f<0\}$ and $\{f>0\}$ are congruent, then in the generic genus-$3$ situation every topological number $L$ satisfies $\langle L,2v\rangle\equiv1\pmod2$. The mechanism is that the electron/hole type of a null-homologous closed trajectory is invariant under the period lattice and is reversed by $\tau$. For $f=\cos2\pi x+\cos2\pi y+\cos2\pi z$ and the $\mu$-cube, this means that the sum of the components of each soul is odd.

metadata.title: Curvature measures and volume preserving flows in h-convex geometry
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a concept of modified curvature measures for h-convex domains in hyperbolic space and prove a shifted version of the generalized Alexandrov theorem, which characterizes geodesic balls in hyperbolic space via modified curvature measures. This result generalizes the classical work of Kohlmann (1998). We further investigate a volume-preserving shifted $\alpha$-Gauss curvature flow for strictly h-convex hypersurfaces in hyperbolic space and prove that for any $\alpha>0$ the solution exists for all time and converges smoothly to a geodesic sphere. The theory of modified curvature measures developed in the first part serves as a key ingredient in characterizing the Hausdorff limit shape of the flow.

metadata.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers
metadata.abstract: We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$. The original proof used the amenability of the images of sufficiently small local fundamental groups. Since that work was written, Kapovitch and Wilking proved Gromov's generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Their theorem gives the stronger conclusion that these local groups are uniformly virtually nilpotent. We explain how their result supplies a direct modern input for the bounded Betti number theorem. We also discuss the topological meaning of the bounded part of ordinary cohomology and its relation to the $\ell^1$-seminorm on homology.

metadata.title: A sharp pinching theorem for closed minimal Legendrian submanifolds
metadata.abstract: Let $F:M^n\to\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$ be a minimal Legendrian immersion of a connected closed manifold, where $n\ge3$, and let $B$ be its second fundamental form. We prove that if $|B|^2\le(n-1)(n+2)/n$, then, up to a unitary transformation, $F$ parametrizes a totally geodesic sphere or is a finite covering of the image of the minimal Calabi product of a point and a totally geodesic Legendrian sphere. This proves Conjecture 1 of Luo and Sun [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré C Anal. Non Linéaire 40 (2023), p. 548].

metadata.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
metadata.abstract: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.

metadata.title: Generic boundary behavior of Dirichlet eigenfunctions
metadata.abstract: We extend Uhlenbeck's classical results on the generic properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions. In particular, we find a residual set of $C^k$ domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $k > n$, such that the nodal set of any Dirichlet eigenfunction intersects the boundary orthogonally along a $C^{k-1}$ embedded submanifold, whenever the intersection is non-empty. This is achieved by analyzing the boundary asymptotics of Dirichlet eigenfunctions via homogeneous harmonic polynomials and comparing their respective nodal sets. Along the way, we give a complete proof that generic Euclidean domains have simple Dirichlet eigenfunctions with zero as a regular value in the interior and zero as a regular value of the boundary normal derivative. In the special case of planar domains, a different argument provides one-parameter families of perturbed domains with the desired properties.

metadata.title: Odd-dimensional lens-space Yamabe counterexamples
metadata.abstract: Let $n\ge5$ be odd and let \(L_{3q}^n=S^n/C_{3q}\) be the standard lens space, where $q>3$ is prime. We prove that for all sufficiently large $q$, \[ \sigma(L_{3q}^n) > (3q)^{-2/n}Y(S^n)=Y(L_{3q}^n,[g_{\rm rd}]). \] Here \([g_{\rm rd}]\) denotes the quotient-round conformal class. Combining spin bordism with the surgery theorem of Ammann--Dahl--Humbert, we establish \[ \sigma(L_{3q}^n)\ge \min \{q^{-2/n}Y(S^n),\Lambda_n\}, \] where $\Lambda_n>0$ depends only on $n$. For sufficiently large $q$, this exceeds the quotient-round value, showing that the quotient-round conformal class need not maximize the smooth Yamabe invariant in any odd dimension $n\ge5$.

analysisBasis.abstract: Let $n\ge5$ be odd and let \(L_{3q}^n=S^n/C_{3q}\) be the standard lens space, where $q>3$ is prime. We prove that for all sufficiently large $q$, \[ \sigma(L_{3q}^n) > (3q)^{-2/n}Y(S^n)=Y(L_{3q}^n,[g_{\rm rd}]). \] Here \([g_{\rm rd}]\) denotes the quotient-round conformal class. Combining spin bordism with the surgery theorem of Ammann--Dahl--Humbert, we establish \[ \sigma(L_{3q}^n)\ge \min \{q^{-2/n}Y(S^n),\Lambda_n\}, \] where $\Lambda_n>0$ depends only on $n$. For sufficiently large $q$, this exceeds the quotient-round value, showing that the quotient-round conformal class need not maximize the smooth Yamabe invariant in any odd dimension $n\ge5$.

metadata.title: Generalized minimizers for the capillarity energy outside convex obstacles
metadata.abstract: In general, the capillarity energy outside an unbounded obstacle may fail to admit volume-constrained minimizers, as infimizing sequences may escape to infinity. We study this minimization problem outside a closed convex obstacle $C$. Via a $\Gamma$-convergence result for the capillarity energies outside sequences of closed convex obstacles converging in the Hausdorff sense, we prove that the infimum of the functional is attained by a generalized minimizer, namely, a finite union of regions, each of which minimizes the capillarity energy outside a limit of translations of $C$ in its volume class, with the total volume satisfying the prescribed constraint. Each generalized minimizer can be suitably approximated by an infimizing sequence, thus providing a description of its asymptotic behaviour. As an application, we study the isoperimetric profile associated with the capillarity energy and investigate how the asymptotic geometry of the obstacle affects both this profile and generalized minimizers and their connectedness.

metadata.title: Smooth approximation, Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities and curvature flows for h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
metadata.abstract: We associate each h-convex body in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}(n\geq 2)$ with a Radon measure valued $(0,2)$-tensor on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ through its horospherical function. Using spherical convolution, we prove that any h-convex body can be approximated by a sequence of smooth strictly h-convex bodies in the Hausdorff sense. This approximation result extends the inequality parts of the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality to general h-convex bodies, but equality rigidity cannot be obtained directly. We prove that the equality holds in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality if and only if the h-convex bodies are geodesic balls. For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which implies the equality rigidity of the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. For the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we introduce a class of globally constrained $k$-th modified quermassintegrals preserving flows with general h-convex initial hypersurfaces to obtain the equality rigidity. Moreover, we prove the flows above preserve h-convexity, make the $(k+1)$-th modified quermassintegrals non-increasing and converge to geodesic spheres. We prove a rigidity theorem for modified area measures for h-convex bodies and use this rigidity theorem to characterize the geodesic balls via modified support measures for h-convex bodies, from which we prove that the $(k+1)$-th modified quermassintegrals strictly decrease in a short time along the flows with non-spherical initial hypersurfaces. Then we obtain the equality rigidity of the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.

metadata.title: On plank coverings of cube annuli
metadata.abstract: We study plank coverings of cube annuli $Q\setminus\delta Q\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, where $Q$ is the $d$-dimensional unit cube and $\delta Q$ is a homothetic copy lying in its interior. A. Bezdek proved that, in dimension $2$, every plank covering of such an annulus has total width at least~1 whenever $\delta\le1-1/\sqrt2$. Smurov, Bogataya, and Bogatyi extended this result to all $d\ge2$ under the condition $\delta\le1-1/\sqrt d$. It is conjectured that the same lower bound holds for $\delta\le1-1/d$. We provide evidence for this conjecture in dimensions $2$ and $3$ by proving that there exist positive constants $\varepsilon_2$ and $\varepsilon_3$ such that the bound remains valid whenever $\delta\le1-1/\sqrt d+\varepsilon_d$.

metadata.title: Stably exotic knotted surfaces up to equivalence
metadata.abstract: In this short note we show the existence of stably exotic knotted surfaces in 4-manifolds in the sense that the embedded surfaces are topologically equivalent but are not smoothly equivalent even after any number of internal and external stabilisations.

metadata.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
metadata.abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product Kähler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.

metadata.title: Sharp Yamabe Bounds for Spherical Three-Space Forms via Four-Dimensional Poincaré--Einstein Compactness
metadata.abstract: Let $\Gamma<SO(4)$ be a nontrivial finite group acting freely on $S^3$, and let $M=S^3/\Gamma$. We prove that every smooth conformal class $C$ on $M$ satisfies \[ Y(M,C)\le |\Gamma|^{-2/3}Y(S^3), \] with equality for the quotient-round conformal class. Consequently, \[ \sigma(M)=|\Gamma|^{-2/3}Y(S^3). \] Our approach uses four-dimensional Poincaré--Einstein fillings of the ball. We first establish compactness for fillings whose conformal infinities range over a compact family of positive-scalar-curvature metrics. Since compactness alone does not guarantee continuation through degenerate Einstein metrics, we use equivariant Fredholm parity to obtain a filling with the prescribed boundary conformal class and group action. A common interior fixed point then makes the Li--Qing--Shi boundary test function invariant, and its descent to $M$ gives the sharp covering factor.

metadata.title: The Links--Gould polynomial of an alternating link is alternating
metadata.abstract: Building on work of Kauffman--Saleur and earlier work of the second author, we derive a determinant formula for the Links--Gould polynomial of links. metadata.title: Exterior free-boundary minimal surfaces of every topological type with at least two ends
metadata.abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface in the complement of the open unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. We prove that for all integers $\ell\geq2$, $b\geq1$ and $\gamma\geq0$ there is a connected, orientable, properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with $\ell$ ends, $b$ boundary components and genus $\gamma$. Its total curvature is finite, and its ends are parallel catenoidal ends of multiplicity one. By the theorem of Mazet and Mendes, a surface of this kind with one end is a rotational annulus. Hence the topological types of such embedded surfaces are exactly the annulus with one end and all types with at least two ends. There are two gluing constructions. For $\ell\geq3$ we stack $\ell$ sheets over a stable catenoidal annulus that meets the sphere along a circle of radius $4/5$, and we join adjacent sheets by half-catenoidal bridges sitting on the sphere. The sheets are small normal graphs over this annulus whose displacements contain different multiples of the Jacobi field of the family of such annuli, so their boundary circles and the logarithmic growth of their ends differ slightly. For $\ell=2$ we double a catenoidal annulus near the critical angle $\pi/4$, where it acquires a bounded rotationally invariant Jacobi field; the distance to the critical annulus is coupled to the size of the bridges. In gluing constructions inside the unit ball that double or stack a compact surface, the bridges themselves must balance the sheets, which forces many bridges. Here the logarithmic growth of the ends absorbs this balancing. A fixed number of bridges therefore suffices, and every topological type is reached, including the small ones.

analysisBasis.abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface in the complement of the open unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. We prove that for all integers $\ell\geq2$, $b\geq1$ and $\gamma\geq0$ there is a connected, orientable, properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with $\ell$ ends, $b$ boundary components and genus $\gamma$. Its total curvature is finite, and its ends are parallel catenoidal ends of multiplicity one. By the theorem of Mazet and Mendes, a surface of this kind with one end is a rotational annulus. Hence the topological types of such embedded surfaces are exactly the annulus with one end and all types with at least two ends. There are two gluing constructions. For $\ell\geq3$ we stack $\ell$ sheets over a stable catenoidal annulus that meets the sphere along a circle of radius $4/5$, and we join adjacent sheets by half-catenoidal bridges sitting on the sphere. The sheets are small normal graphs over this annulus whose displacements contain different multiples of the Jacobi field of the family of such annuli, so their boundary circles and the logarithmic growth of their ends differ slightly. For $\ell=2$ we double a catenoidal annulus near the critical angle $\pi/4$, where it acquires a bounded rotationally invariant Jacobi field; the distance to the critical annulus is coupled to the size of the bridges. In gluing constructions inside the unit ball that double or stack a compact surface, the bridges themselves must balance the sheets, which forces many bridges. Here the logarithmic growth of the ends absorbs this balancing. A fixed number of bridges therefore suffices, and every topological type is reached, including the small ones.

metadata.title: Arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds with bounded rank
metadata.abstract: We prove that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $n$-manifolds of bounded rank have bounded adjoint trace field degree, and consequently have lower bounded injectivity radius. From this, we obtain a number of corollaries. In particular, we obtain that closed arithmetic hyperbolic $3$-manifolds of bounded rank are contained in finitely many commensurability classes, and describe these commensurability classes. Additionally, it follows that for closed arithmetic hyperbolic $3$-manifolds, Heegaard genus is equal to rank for all but finitely many manifolds of each rank.

analysis.progressType: 秩有界算术双曲流形的有限性
analysis.workSummary: 证明闭算术双曲 n 维流形的基本群秩有界时，其伴随迹域次数有界，因而单射半径有统一正下界。三维时进一步得到有限多个可公度类并描述它们，且每个固定秩下除有限例外外 Heegaard 亏格等于秩。
analysis.breakthrough: 把群秩约束转化为算术与局部几何控制，并连接三维 Heegaard 亏格。
analysis.limitations: 要求闭且算术；可公度有限性及 Heegaard 结论为三维结果，后者允许每个秩有限例外。
analysis.priorityReason: 双曲几何群论及三维拓扑的重要统一控制
